"However, in this case, the work that the girls are putting in is futile. My daughter and her teammates feel defeated because they know the physical advantage that males have over females. They often have to listen as male coaches praise the [alleged biological male athlete’s] athletic ability, all the while these girls knowing that [the alleged biological male athlete] has unfair physical advantages.

"As a society that allows boys into girls’ private spaces, we are sending the young women a message that they will never be good enough, that the scholarships will probably never go to them, and that in general, being a female, is at best, only good enough to stand in 2nd place, behind the boys who you never had a chance at beating in the first place. As adults, we are failing to keep our young girls safe.

"As parents of athletes, we have a responsibility to raise our girls to be proud of being female, proud of being strong in mind and body, and proud to stand for the rights of all women and girls, both on the court and off. We cannot allow these violations to continue. Women were granted these rights under Title IX, and the law is being violated by USA Volleyball! Women and girls and their advocates should not have to continue to fight for rights that were already given to them!"

"As a female athlete who loves playing volleyball, I never thought or could have ever imagined I would have to be put in a situation where I would have to compete with and against an [alleged] boy.

"Seeing an [alleged] boy jump higher and hit harder while seeing [the alleged biological male athlete] get recognized over me was extremely humiliating as a female athlete. No matter how hard I worked at getting better, I knew I could never be as good as [the alleged biological male athlete]. Volleyball nets are higher in men’s volleyball due to this reason.

"I trusted USA Volleyball and leadership members who run volleyball club organizations to protect me and my fellow female athletes. Instead, I have lost trust in these adults and organizations. Knowing [alleged] male athletes are playing under the USA Volleyball guidelines and sweeping it under the rug makes me feel defeated as a young female. I have worked so hard to get to where I am, and allowing an [alleged] boy to play on an all-girls volleyball team has me discouraged to even keep playing the sport I love.

"USA Volleyball states 'compete in the gender matching the sex assigned at birth on their birth certificate.' Well in my state you can change your gender with the identity you identify as. How is this fair? Due to your guidelines and rules, I have to compete with an [alleged] biological male because they can amend their birth certificate to FEMALE. This is not fair or safe for me and the rest of female athletes."

"As a mother of a female athlete whose daughter had to play on the same team as an [alleged] biological male, I believe USA Volleyball should have clear, consistent methods for verifying athlete eligibility. The current USA Volleyball policy states that 'USAV athlete members are expected to participate or compete in all USAV-sanctioned events or activities as a member of the gender assigned at the time of birth on their birth certificate.'

TRANS ATHLETES DROP LAWSUIT TO GAIN ACCESS TO GIRLS' SPORTS IN NEW HAMPSHIRE AFTER SCOTUS RULING

"As a parent of a female athlete, it is frustrating when the rules are not being applied consistently. In some states, birth certificates can be amended to reflect a person’s gender identity.

"This creates uncertainty when eligibility rules are intended to be based on biological sex at birth. In competitions where eligibility is based on biological sex, we believe USA Volleyball needs to consider additional methods of verification so that the rules are applied consistently to every athlete and all competitors are treated fairly. I witnessed firsthand what my daughter and her teammates experienced.

"They felt humiliated and discouraged when an [alleged] male athlete had physical advantages in jumping and hitting power that the girls could not match. They also felt disheartened when those abilities received recognition. Men’s volleyball is played with a higher net, reflecting recognized physical differences between the men’s and women’s games. I watched my daughter’s confidence decline because she believed the eligibility rules were not being enforced consistently.

"She felt there was no meaningful way to ensure that the policy was applied as written. USA Volleyball needs to do more to protect fair competition for female athletes. Solely relying on birth certificates alone is not sufficient enough to verify eligibility under a policy that is intended to be based on sex assigned at birth."

"As a father, I was outraged. I trusted that if USA Volleyball had eligibility rules, they would be enforced consistently. Instead, I watched my daughter and her teammates compete in a situation they believed did not follow those rules. USA volleyball said they wouldn’t remove the [alleged biological male] athlete because of an amended birth certificate, even though the policy is based on sex assigned at birth.

"I was given a meeting after requesting one with the leadership of my daughter’s local volleyball team to discuss concerns regarding an [alleged] male athlete participating on her girls’ team. During the meeting, information was presented that demonstrated the athlete was [allegedly] biologically male.

"Despite the evidence provided, the team leadership stated that they had been instructed by both their regional governing organization and USA Volleyball to accept the athlete’s amended birth certificate as the determining document for eligibility. As a result, my concerns were dismissed, and no further action was taken by the organization regarding the matter. Her local club team was not only made aware of the [alleged biological male athlete] being in the team but was also told by numerous other parents on her team along with opposing team parents and coaches and they still turned a blind eye.

"What made me the angriest was watching my daughter pay the price. My daughter lost confidence, felt like her concerns were dismissed, and started questioning whether the rules actually meant anything. As a father, there’s nothing more frustrating than seeing your child speak up, believe she’s standing up for what’s right, and feel like no one is willing to listen.

"This isn’t about hate or attacking anyone personally. It’s about fairness, accountability, and expecting organizations to enforce the policies they put in place. If the rules are going to exist, they should be applied consistently to every athlete. That’s all we’ve ever asked for."

Fox News Digital has reached out to USA Volleyball for a response to the family's statements.

Jackson Thompson is a sports reporter for Fox News Digital covering critical political and cultural issues in sports, with an investigative lens. Jackson's reporting has been cited in federal government actions related to the enforcement of Title IX, and in legacy media outlets including The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer, The Associated Press and ESPN.com.

articles.title: Biden's battle with advancing cancer renews focus on prostate disease
articles.excerpt: Fox News contributor Karl Rove and former Biden 2020 campaign surrogate Kevin Walling discuss former President Joe Biden’s prostate cancer diagnosis and allegations of a cover-up by the Democratic Par...
articles.body_text:
Fox News contributor Karl Rove and former Biden 2020 campaign surrogate Kevin Walling discuss former President Joe Biden’s prostate cancer diagnosis and allegations of a cover-up by the Democratic Party on ‘The Story.’

Former President Joe Biden’s prostate cancer has spread further since his diagnosis last year, his son Hunter Biden revealed in a BBC interview that aired Friday.

"The cancer has spread, metastasized into his bones and further," Hunter Biden told BBC Newsnight, describing his father’s condition as "very painful" and "very debilitating in many respects."

"It’s really sad to watch," the younger Biden went on. "The only thing that I’d say about my dad, about his health right now, is I wish he would complain more, because it’s not good."

JOE BIDEN'S CANCER HAS SPREAD FURTHER, LEAVING HIM IN 'VERY PAINFUL' CONDITION, HUNTER REVEALS

Biden, 83, announced his diagnosis in May 2025, after news that a "small nodule" had been found in the former president's prostate during a routine exam.

"While this represents a more aggressive form of the disease, the cancer appears to be hormone-sensitive, which allows for effective management," his office said at the time. "The president and his family are reviewing treatment options with his physicians."

Former President Joe Biden’s prostate cancer has spread further since his diagnosis last year, his son Hunter Biden revealed. (Getty Images)

Biden later underwent hormone therapy and radiation treatment, completing a course of radiation at Penn Medicine Radiation Oncology in Philadelphia in October 2025, according to the former president's spokesperson.

In addition to hormone therapy, common treatment options for prostate cancer include chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy and radiopharmaceutical treatments.

Fox News Digital reached out to Biden's office for comment.

Prostate cancer is a disease found in men that develops in the prostate gland. Cases have been on the rise in recent years, with overall incidence increasing about 3% annually from 2014 through 2021, according to the American Cancer Society.

Rates of advanced-stage prostate cancer rose about 5% per year during that period.

NEW BLOOD TEST DETECTS 90% OF AGGRESSIVE PROSTATE CANCER CASES, BEATING CURRENT SCREENINGS

About 333,830 new cases of prostate cancer are expected to be diagnosed in the U.S. in 2026, and about 36,320 men are expected to die from the disease, according to the American Cancer Society.

One in eight men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer in their lifetime, the same source stated.

Older men are at a higher risk of the disease, with six in 10 cases diagnosed in patients 65 and older. The average age at diagnosis is 67, with men under 40 rarely affected.

Prostate cancer is the second-most common cancer in men, behind only skin cancer, the ACS noted.

Among men who undergo routine prostate cancer screening, the disease is usually caught early before symptoms emerge, per the ACS.

Typical early symptoms include problems urinating, a weak or slow urinary stream or an increased need to urinate. Some men may also notice blood in the urine or bodily fluids.

Biden, 83, announced his diagnosis in May 2025, after news that a "small nodule" had been found in the former president's prostate during a routine exam. (AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin, File)

More advanced symptoms may occur after the disease has spread. Those may include pain in the hips, back (spine), chest (ribs) or other areas, the ACS stated.

Men may also suffer from erectile dysfunction, weight loss, extreme fatigue, weakness in the legs or feet, or loss of bladder or bowel control.

The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force states that men aged 55 to 69 years should have the option to undergo periodic prostate-specific antigen (PSA)-based screening to monitor for prostate cancer.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Before deciding whether to be screened, men should have an opportunity to discuss the potential benefits and harms of screening with their clinician and to incorporate their values and preferences in the decision," the USPSTF states.

The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force states that men aged 55 to 69 years should have the option to undergo periodic prostate-specific antigen (PSA)-based screening to monitor for prostate cancer. (iStock)

While screening offers a "small potential benefit" of reducing the chances of dying from the disease, the agency noted that some men may experience negative effects, including false-positive results, overdiagnosis and overtreatment, and treatment complications.

Alternative prostate cancer screening methods are currently being researched, including one that uses a non-invasive urine test, as Fox News Digital recently reported.

For localized prostate cancers, where the disease is contained within the prostate, the five-year survival rate is at least 99%, according to the ACS.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

For regional cases, where the disease has spread only to "nearby structures or lymph nodes," the five-year survival rate is also 99% or greater.

If the cancer has spread to other areas of the body, the five-year survival rate drops to 37%.

Actual survival rates may vary based on the patient's age, overall health, how the cancer has progressed post-diagnosis, the disease's response to treatment, and other factors, the ACS noted.

Melissa Rudy is senior health editor and a member of the lifestyle team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to melissa.rudy@fox.com.

articles.title: National Indigenous Music awards 2026: Baker Boy wins big, including album and song of the year
articles.excerpt:
Yolŋu hip-hop artist dominates, while Butchulla duo and cousins Birdz and Fred Leone win artist of the year and Drifting Clouds takes home best new talent

Baker Boy has won album, song and film clip ...
articles.body_text:
Yolŋu hip-hop artist dominates, while Butchulla duo and cousins Birdz and Fred Leone win artist of the year and Drifting Clouds takes home best new talent

Baker Boy has won album, song and film clip of the year at the 2026 National Indigenous music awards (Nimas), paying tribute to his late grandmother who his sophomore album, Djandjay, is named for.

The Yolŋu hip-hop artist, whose name is Danzal Baker, won three awards for Djandjay, including song of the year and film clip of the year for its hit single Thick Skin, which features Indigenous artists Thelma Plum, Emma Donovan, Kee’ahn and Jada Weazel.

Djandjay marks an evolution from Baker’s 2021 debut, Gela, delivering deeper lyrical themes and a heavier sound.

“[Djandjay] has the lyricism, the play on words, the whole thing,” he told Guardian Australia backstage at the Nimas. “I would say the persona and the whole Blak look has a very staunch feel, and that vulnerability as well.”

Accepting album of the year, Baker dedicated the honour to his late grandmother, whom he credits with bringing hip-hop to Arnhem Land after returning from a Los Angeles honeymoon with vinyl records and VHS tapes. These inspired his father and uncle to form 1980s dance duo the Baker Boys.

“She was the reason that I have confidence and have no shame to be able to get out there and express my feelings, and who I am and where I come from,” Baker said.

Baker told Guardian Australia he wrote Thick Skin, which won song and film clip of the year, following the voice to parliament referendum.

“I was in the middle of working on the album and there was like a brick wall that was happening right in front of me … I had to speak my voice,” he said.

The music video was filmed at the colonial-era Werribee Mansion in Victoria. “Filming somewhere with that colonialism, taking back that authority and giving a ‘this is my house’ vibe,” Baker told Guardian Australia. “It’s about POC [people of colour] and Blak excellence – having white butlers and flipping that sort of feel.”

Artist of the year was awarded to Butchulla duo Birdz and Fred Leone. The cousins – rapper Birdz and songman Leone – released a joint six-track EP titled Gira in 2025.

“I grew up in Katherine and this territory really shaped me and inspires me still today. So, thank you, thank you, thank you,” Birdz said, accepting the award with Leone by his side.

Yolŋu musician Drifting Clouds, whose name is Terry Guyula, took home best new talent. Known for his synth-driven tracks with Yolŋu Matha lyrics, Guyula accepted the award alongside producer and bandmate Zac Terry, whom Guyula thanked for “bringing me out from the bush to the city.”

Guguyelandji and Woppaburra jazz and blues musician Marlene Cummins and Galiwin’ku’s Saltwater Band were inducted into the Nimas Hall of Fame, joining the likes of Jessica Mauboy and Yothu Yindi.

Baker Boy told Guardian Australia he was “very proud” to see Saltwater Band inducted, having grown up listening to them, saying: “When I was a kid on [Milingimbi] island, they would come perform and I’d be up there dancing.”

Mauboy presented Saltwater Band with their award, praising their three-decade legacy of blending traditional Yolŋu song with reggae, ska and contemporary music.

“It fills me with pride to celebrate music from the Northern Territory,” Mauboy said. “Saltwater Band created a sound that was completely their own … they showed artists like me and so many young people watching that you never have to leave your culture to chase your dreams. You can carry it with you.”

Song of the year: Baker Boy – Thick Skin (feat. Thelma Plum, Emma Donovan, Kee’ahn & Jada Weazel)

Film clip of the year: Baker Boy – Thick Skin (feat. Thelma Plum, Emma Donovan, Kee’ahn & Jada Weazel)

Community clip of the year: Northern Peninsula Area – All The Way From The NPA

Indigenous language award: Bulman School & Community – Lok Lok Mah Burarr (Lizard & Goanna)

Hall of fame inductions: Marlene Cummins and Saltwater Band

Guardian Australia travelled to Darwin courtesy of Tourism NT

articles.title: Flight canceled after toddler refused to buckle seat belt, stranding passengers overnight
articles.excerpt: Video shows the aftermath of a disruptive passenger incident aboard United Flight 1364, where retired Minneapolis Police Chief Brian O'Hara joined two off-duty law enforcement officers to help restrai...
articles.body_text:
Video shows the aftermath of a disruptive passenger incident aboard United Flight 1364, where retired Minneapolis Police Chief Brian O'Hara joined two off-duty law enforcement officers to help restrain the man until the plane landed safely. Credit: Wafiyyah O'Hara

An evening flight from British Columbia to Toronto this week had to be canceled because a toddler refused to buckle their seat belt, the airline confirmed to Fox News Digital.

Porter Airlines flight 444 was expected to leave from Victoria International Airport at 10:30 p.m. and had begun taxiing when a flight attendant noticed the child.

"A young child was standing in their seat and would not secure their seatbelt," the airline shared with Fox News Digital in a statement, adding that neither the adult with the child nor the crew were able to get the child buckled.

FLIGHT PASSENGER BLASTS 'INCOMPETENT PARENTS' AFTER UNRULY CHILD FORCES PLANE DELAY

Porter Airlines flight 444 was expected to leave from Victoria International Airport in British Columbia, but a young child had other ideas. (NurPhoto via Getty Images, File)

"The aircraft could not take off in this unsafe condition, so the crew elected to return to the terminal and have the passengers disembark," the airline added.

Because the airport has a takeoff curfew of 12:30 a.m., and it took time to get the passengers in question and their luggage off the plane and do the necessary paperwork, the flight had to be canceled, and the other passengers had to stay the night.

'WE THOUGHT WE WOULD DIE': PASSENGERS THROWN INTO CEILING DURING TERRIFYING FLIGHT

Victoria International Airport's runway closes at 12:30 p.m. (AFP via Getty Images)

The other passengers were rebooked on a Friday flight.

"We apologize for the effect this had on other passengers," Porter added.

The delayed passengers finally left the airport on Friday. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)

A child safety seat or restraint device is required for children under two flying on the airline. It’s unclear how old the child was.

Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Will Pakistan-Saudi-Turkiye defence pact change US strategy?
articles.excerpt: Washington, DC – The administration of United States President Donald Trump has offered no official response in the hours since Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan signed a landmark mutual defence agre...
articles.body_text:
Washington, DC – The administration of United States President Donald Trump has offered no official response in the hours since Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan signed a landmark mutual defence agreement in Mecca.

The muted reaction, which persisted into Saturday, likely underscores the multilayered — and still emerging — implications of the new deal for US strategy, according to analysts.

Considered by many to lay the groundwork for what could be one of the most significant power shifts in the region in decades, the deal comes within the context of the US-Israeli war against Iran and Israel’s increasingly aggressive military actions in the region.

One provision is said to call on signatories to treat an attack on one as an attack on all, reminiscent of NATO’s Article 5.

Some analysts see the agreement as a reflection of growing wariness towards an unpredictable US government, potentially presaging a wider security realignment that could transform the Middle East.

Others have argued that, while US actions have indeed fostered the conditions that accelerated the deal, the pact fits neatly within US strategic aims of greater burden-sharing among allies.

In the near term, many experts agree the pact will likely have the greatest impact in the diplomatic sphere, posing a potentially insurmountable challenge to Arab-Israeli normalisation under the Abraham Accords.

The push for greater regional cooperation with Israel has been the linchpin of the Trump administration’s designs for the Middle East, dating back to his first term. But Sina Toosi, a senior fellow at the Centre for International Policy, explained that the mutual defence pact is likely a setback.

“Ironically, the US and Israel entered the war [with Iran] hoping to reshape the regional balance of power in Israel’s favour and accelerate regional integration through initiatives like the Abraham Accords,” Toosi told Al Jazeera.

“Instead, one of the first major post-war developments is the emergence of a defence initiative among three major Muslim powers seeking greater strategic autonomy.”

The full details of the agreement have not yet been released. Only a joint statement on Friday has addressed the pact’s terms.

The central pledge of the agreement “stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all”, according to the statement. But that premise remains so far untested.

The pact builds on a previous mutual defence agreement with a similar provision, reached between Saudi Arabia and Pakistan in September 2025. It came just days after Israel launched an air strike on the Qatari capital Doha, exacerbating concerns about Washington’s ability to control one of its closest allies.

In the wake of the Hamas-led attacks on October 7, 2023, Israel has led multiple war efforts, including against Iran, Lebanon and a genocidal campaign in Gaza.

Officials in Riyadh, Ankara and Islamabad have taken pains to stress that Friday’s agreement is meant to supplement, not supplant, any other alliances. Experts have further cautioned that the strengthening of defence ties between the trio does paper over their individual, and at times diverging, interests.

Saudi Arabia, for instance, said the deal “does not represent any orientation toward building a military axis or sectarian/religious bloc”.

“The agreement does not come at the expense of the Kingdom’s strategic and strong relations at the Gulf, Arab, and international levels,” it said.

The country has been the target of a large number of Iran’s retaliatory attacks since the US-Israeli war began on February 28, and more recently, it has seen increased strikes from the Houthis in Yemen and Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq.

Meanwhile, Turkiye’s presidential communication directorate said the strengthened partnership “is not an alternative” to the country’s membership in the 32-country NATO bloc.

Indeed, experts have said the agreement does not appear to have any bearing on any NATO commitments, although it could eventually lead to a diversion of resources in the event of multiple escalations.

Turkiye has the second-largest standing army in NATO, as well as access to advanced military technology. Saudi Arabia is understood as bringing its vast power of the purse to the agreement. Pakistan is the only nuclear-armed power of the three.

Despite assurances that the pact is not a regional re-orientation, some observers have connected the new alliance to the Trump administration’s at-times caustic approach towards NATO and its wider pivot away from multilateralism.

They argue it represents a clear, if nascent, weakening of Washington’s strategic sway.

“The basis for our alliance in the Middle East, in the Persian Gulf, and certainly with NATO and with our allies in Asia, have been shaken,” Harlan Ullman, the chairman of the Killowen Group advisory firm and a former naval officer, told Al Jazeera in a television interview.

“How badly remains to be seen. It may only be stirred, not shaken. But it’s something that we need to worry about.”

The US approach to the Gulf has largely been based on forging military, economic and diplomatic ties in the region. In turn, Gulf states have expected de facto security guarantees.

That strategy was energised in the early 1980s upon the founding of the Gulf Cooperation Council, and it grew amid the US invasion of Iraq and Afghanistan, part of Washington’s so-called “global war on terror”.

The US has about 50,000 troops stationed across 19 sites in the Middle East, with US-controlled bases in Turkiye, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar and the UAE, and a presence at bases in Saudi Arabia, Oman, Jordan, Iraq and Israel.

Qatar, Bahrain, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Egypt are among the countries in the region that the US has designated as “major non-NATO allies”, underscoring the importance of their military and economic ties. Pakistan is also a major non-NATO ally.

But critics have argued the US-Israeli war with Iran has degraded the foundations of those alliances.

Nawaf Obaid, a senior fellow at the Department of War Studies at King’s College London, has characterised the Pakistan-Saudi-Turkiye deal as the clearest sign yet of the shift away from an “American-designed regional security order”.

“The US-Iran war accelerated a transformation already under way,” Obaid argued in a column for Al Jazeera.

He pointed out that hosting US bases has made several Gulf states targets for attacks during the ongoing war with Iran.

“Iranian retaliatory strikes exposed the vulnerability of the US basing structure in the Gulf and forced the repositioning of substantial combat forces,” Obaid said.

The loosening bonds can also be seen on the US side. Successive administrations — including those led by former Presidents Barack Obama and Joe Biden — have attempted to pivot away from the Middle East, pursuing instead a renewed emphasis on China and the Asia Pacific.

The 2025 National Security Strategy, early in Trump’s second term, gave only brief mention to the region.

While Washington’s “intelligence relationships, military power, technology and economic influence will remain formidable” in the region, Obaid predicts the US presence will wane.

“Several American bases will eventually close, as they have lost strategic utility,” he wrote.

Asli Aydintasbas, a fellow at the Brookings Institution, also pointed to a desire within the Trump administration to shift away from the Middle East, particularly when it comes to so-called “democracy building”.

But that desire has generally not extended to withdrawing military forces in the Gulf, she explained. With efforts to end the five-month war in Iran repeatedly stalled, any short-term change in the US military posture remains unlikely.

“Now there’s a hot war in the Middle East. Obviously, it’s not really the time to pull US troops or commitments,” Aydintasbas said.

“On the other hand, we’ve also seen the limits of US deterrence in the region in the form of Iranian attacks on US allies and Iran’s continuing ability to inflict pain on US allies and global trade, despite its weaker military model.”

Aydintasbas is among experts who believe that Washington likely sees the new security agreement as in line with its calls for more burden-sharing among allies.

The Trump administration has been dogged by reports of munitions shortages during the war with Iran, and it has called on its allies, particularly in NATO, to crank up their military spending.

“I think the United States is not bothered by a deal among three close US allies for their own protection. It is consistent with the Trump administration’s ideas on burden-sharing and regional solutions,” she said.

Aydintasbas also questioned whether Turkiye or Pakistan would indeed retaliate against the Houthis or Iran in response to attacks on Saudi Arabia, under the terms of the pact.

“It also really is an agreement that has its own limits, and US officials know that full well,” she added.

Burcu Ozcelik, a senior research fellow for Middle East security at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), also said she would “resist reading this as evidence of a post-American Middle East”.

“If anything, it fits the broader US preference for greater regional burden-sharing, regional powers assuming more responsibility for deterrence and security while remaining embedded, to different degrees, within a US-centred security architecture,” she wrote in a post on the social media platform X.

“Stronger regional security cooperation among US partners is entirely compatible with the direction of American strategy.”

While Friday’s mutual defence deal may not shift US military strategy in the foreseeable future, the agreement appears to send a potent message about the normalisation of regional ties with Israel under the Abraham Accords.

That push has been a cornerstone of the Trump administration’s diplomatic approach to the Middle East: Trump oversaw the UAE, Bahrain and Morocco signing onto the accords during his first term.

Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, however, derailed any recent progress on the effort, which was already criticised for sidelining the issue of Palestinian peace and statehood.

Normalising Saudi Arabia-Israel relations has long been a crowning, if elusive, goal for the Trump administration. But experts say the Pakistan-Turkiye-Saudi Arabia deal puts the prospect of expanding the Abraham Accords further out of reach, if not sounding a death knell altogether.

That is particularly true after Trump retroactively made joining the Abraham Accords a condition for the sale of nuclear reactors to Saudi Arabia, according to defence analyst Alex Alfirraz Scheers.

“I think the fact that the president of the United States basically said that the Saudi nuclear cooperation agreement was contingent on the Saudis joining the Abraham Accords certainly sounded alarms all across the Gulf,” Alfirraz Scheers told Al Jazeera in a television interview.

“[It showed] the Abraham Accords are now being used for coercive purposes.”

Aydintasbas, the fellow at the Brookings Institution, said the pact removes any ambiguity about Riyadh’s position.

“This makes it crystal clear that the Saudis are not going to join the Abraham Accords as long as the Palestinian issue remains unresolved,” she said.

articles.title: DiJonai Carrington declares 'White privilege' after ejection for smacking Sophie Cunningham in the face
articles.excerpt:
Dan Dakich breaks down Megan Rapinoe's latest unhinged rant targeting Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham and OutKick legend Riley Gaines over their stand to protect women's sports.

Chicago Sky play...
articles.body_text:
Dan Dakich breaks down Megan Rapinoe's latest unhinged rant targeting Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham and OutKick legend Riley Gaines over their stand to protect women's sports.

Chicago Sky player DiJonai Carrington sent a post on Threads that read "white privilege" and tagged the Indiana Fever after she was ejected from Saturday's game for smacking Sophie Cunningham in the face.

Carrington has previously garnered controversy for poking Cunningham's teammate Caitlin Clark in the eye during the 2024 playoffs, and making controversial statements in the media.

DiJonai Carrington of the Chicago Sky was ejected after a brutal foul on Sophie Cunningham of the Indiana Fever. (Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images)

With about two minutes left in the first quarter, Cunningham had the ball and was headed in for a layup. Carrington was on her tail.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Carrington hustled and got to Cunningham in time, but then delivered a brutal shot straight to the Fever star's head.

The incident prompted Cunningham to get back up and scream at Carrington, as referees had to separate the two players.

Upon review, Carrington's foul was upgraded to a flagrant 2 foul, and she was ejected from the game. Carrington then made the post on Threads shortly after her ejection, presumably from the locker room.

Carrington did not elaborate on the post, leaving unclear whether it referred to Cunningham, the officiating decision or the Fever organization. She also did not accuse Cunningham by name, and there was no immediate evidence that the foul was connected to Cunningham’s position on transgender athletes.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM TAKES VICIOUS ELBOW TO FACE, AND FANS FUME AT WHAT REFS DID NEXT

The collision nevertheless unfolded as Cunningham remained at the center of a widening political debate. Supporters held a fourth rally outside the venue of a Fever road game on Saturday, while counterprotesters also gathered near the United Center.

Sophie Cunningham confronts DiJonai Carrington after the latter committed a hard foul that led to her being ejected in the first quarter of Saturday's game between the Indiana Fever and the Chicago Sky. (Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images)

Cunningham has said she does not harbor hatred toward transgender people but believes protecting girls and women in sports is "common sense." White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt previously defended Cunningham, saying the backlash against her was "astonishing."

With another Cunningham rally already scheduled ahead of the Fever’s Aug. 22 game against the New York Liberty, controversy is bound to surround Cunningham and Indiana beyond Chicago.

Meanwhile, Carrington already had a contentious history with the Fever before Saturday. During the 2024 season, she mocked Caitlin Clark for what she believed was flopping and later called Indiana supporters "the nastiest fans in the W" after receiving racist abuse from some online users.

Carrington then struck Clark in the eye while defending a pass during the 2024 playoffs, leaving the Fever star with a black eye. Both players said the contact was accidental, although Carrington later drew renewed criticism after appearing to joke about the controversy during an Instagram Live video.

Carrington has also responded to accusations that she plays dirty, insisting she simply plays aggressively and always attempts to make a play on the ball. Beyond basketball, she has drawn attention for wearing an explicit anti-President Donald Trump sweatshirt and urging WNBA players to oppose Trump administration policies affecting women and the LGBTQ community.

Jackson Thompson is a sports reporter for Fox News Digital covering critical political and cultural issues in sports, with an investigative lens. Jackson's reporting has been cited in federal government actions related to the enforcement of Title IX, and in legacy media outlets including The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer, The Associated Press and ESPN.com.

articles.title: World’s largest motorcycle rally roars into Sturgis as bikers flood tiny US town
articles.excerpt:
The biggest motorcycle rally in the world started as a place for WW2 vets to find community.

The annual Sturgis Motorcycle Rally is officially underway, with hundreds of thousands of riders descendin...
articles.body_text:
The biggest motorcycle rally in the world started as a place for WW2 vets to find community.

The annual Sturgis Motorcycle Rally is officially underway, with hundreds of thousands of riders descending on the small South Dakota town and surrounding Black Hills regions for the 86th edition of what’s billed as the world’s largest motorcycle rally.

The rally is held annually for ten days in August and involves races, concerts and group rides and typically draws about 500,000 attendees to Sturgis, population 7,100.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

During the rally, Sturgis is transformed as motorcycles pack downtown streets and riders fan out across the Black Hills. The event extends far beyond the city itself, with concerts, races, stunt shows, motorcycle demonstrations, vendor exhibitions and organized rides taking place throughout the region.

This year’s headliner is country star Lainey Wilson, who is set to perform August 12. Other acts on the concert schedule include YUNGBLUD, Megadeth, Lynyrd Skynyrd, Rob Zombie and Insane Clown Posse.

The small town of Sturgis, South Dakota transforms into a bustling city with hundreds of thousands of visitors during the annual Sturgis Motorcycle Rally. (iStock)

Two long-distance women’s motorcycle rides – the Women Riders World Relay and Shantell’s Sisterhood Ride – will conclude at the Sturgis Motorcycle Museum & Hall of Fame’s second-annual Pearl’s Jam event, which celebrates women in motorcycling.

Harley-Davidson announced it would be debuting its new Deadwood motorcycle at this year’s event, "a new model inspired in part by the post-war history of the Sturgis Rally," reported Motor Sports NewsWire.

Indian Motorcycle is also introducing a new bike.

"The new Indian Chief Vintage Sturgis SD Edition celebrates Indian’s place in the rally’s history with special paint and badging inspired by Indians of the 1930s," reported Rider Magazine. "It features a classic two-tone Indian Motorcycle Red and Cream paint with a multicolored Indian Motorcycle headdress logo."

The rally also serves as a jumping-off point for motorcycle rides throughout the Black Hills, with visitors venturing to Mount Rushmore National Memorial, Custer State Park, Badlands National Park, Wind Cave National Park and Bear Butte State Park, along with historic towns such as Deadwood.

Mount Rushmore is a popular riding destination for attendees of the Sturgis Motorcycle Rally. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)

One other attraction Sturgis goes frequently visit is Devils Tower National Monument in Wyoming, a particularly popular motorcycle destination from the Black Hills.

The Sturgis Rally was started by Indian dealer Pappy Hoel in 1938, according to the official Sturgis Rally website.

"Pappy was the man who put the brotherhood in motorcycles," Coe Meyer, a Sturgis motorcycle historian, told Fox News Digital previously. "He’s the reason so many people come here today."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Hoel’s marketing ingenuity, enthusiasm for motorcycle racing and — unbeknownst to many — his paternal fondness for America’s World War II veterans struggling with the mental wounds of combat made Sturgis synonymous with motorcycles, Fox News Digital reported.

"He was like a P.T. Barnum-type character. He always had a trick up his sleeve," said Vinny Terranova, who knew Hoel and his wife Pearl and who operates their original Junction Avenue motorcycle shop today as Pappy’s Vintage Cycles.

Sturgis, South Dakota hosts a motorcycle rally each year that routinely attracts about half-a-million attendees. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)

"He loved motorcycles, loved racing and loved motorcyclists," said Terranova of Pappy Hoel. "He and Pearl always had a pot of beans and franks on the grill. Nobody left hungry."

The Hoels ran the Sturgis Motorcycle Rally for nearly 50 years, before turning it over to the City of Sturgis in the 1980s.

Teresa Mull is a freelance writer with the Lifestyle team at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Australia news live: near miss for Jetstar and Qatar Airways planes taxiing at Sydney airport
articles.excerpt:
Meanwhile, expert says bird flu detected on Murray-Darling basin ‘should be ringing alarm bells’. Follow updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Jetstar pilot was force...
articles.body_text:
Meanwhile, expert says bird flu detected on Murray-Darling basin ‘should be ringing alarm bells’. Follow updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Jetstar pilot was forced to brake suddenly when a Qatar Airways plane came into “close proximity” while the other plane was taxiing at Sydney airport this morning.

Guardian Australia understands a Jetstar cabin crew member was injured in the incident, and was treated by paramedics.

The Jetstar flight from Sydney to the Gold Coast was taxiing out from its bay at Sydney airport this morning when the incident occurred.

double quotation markOur aircraft was following instructions by Air Traffic Control when the pilots were forced to brake firmly after another aircraft came in close proximity.
   We have commenced an investigation into the incident.

The NSW premier, Chris Minns, says he is “concerned” to hear about the near miss incident involving a Jetstar and Qatar Airways plane while taxiing at Sydney airport this morning.

Passengers travelling through Sydney airport have been warned of delays this week due to air traffic controller rostering issues.

Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Minns said he was concerned about potential safety risks and stressed the importance of the airport operating at full capacity:

double quotation markThat’s hugely important for our economy

We’re hopeful that there’s a plan in place to recruit more people for a highly specialised but very important job… we’re opening a brand new airport in the not too distant future, so there’ll be even more strain on that service than there is today. I know it’s hard to employ people, particularly for these specialised services, because we’ve got a very tight labor market. But this isn’t a nice to have; it’s a must have,

AirServices Australia, say departures have been spaced out at Sydney airport after the incident involving a Jetstar and Qatar Airways Plane this morning.

In a statement, a spokesperson for AirServices Australia said:

Airservices Australia has enacted Air Traffic Flow Management (ATFM) measures including departure spacing at Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport to safely manage projected airborne and departure demands following a reported safety incident between two aircraft moving on taxiways.

We are working with airlines to reduce delays and the impact on passenger travel as much as possible.

Airservices is reviewing the incident and will assist with any safety investigation.

Witness describes Jetstar-Qatar near miss at Sydney airport

A witness to the near miss between Jetstar and Qatar Airways planes at Sydney airport has spoken to the ABC.

Dani Brown was on another plane at the Sydney airport tarmac when she witnessed the incident this morning. She told the ABC the plane’s pilot told passengers there was a “traffic congestion issue”:

double quotation markIt was looking like a very close near miss.

Our flight was meant to leave at 7.15 and we just sat at the tarmac at our gate, because it was quite close to the gate. And we just had to wait until the Jetstar plane was towed away and it was clear for us to move. It was a pretty empty flight for us.

Protective services officers to be stationed at major Victorian hospitals under Coalition plan

The Victorian Coalition has pledged to deploy protective services officers (PSOs) to the state’s major hospitals if it wins November’s state election.

The proposal, unveiled on Sunday, aims to reduce violence at hospitals.

In a statement, the Coalition said 70 PSOs would be deployed as part of a two-year pilot at seven major Victorian hospitals.

PSO teams would provide additional security, respond to serious incidents and escort hospital workers to their vehicles, a statement said.

The opposition leader, Jess Wilson, said:

double quotation markDoctors, nurses, and healthcare staff should be able to do their jobs safely so that they can provide Victorians with the care they need.

The state’s shadow health minister, Georgie Crozier, said health workers need “greater protection.”

double quotation markThe safety of our health workers is paramount – you should feel safe, feel protected, whether you are triaging a patient in ED or walking to your car after ending your shift.

A man has been charged over an alleged assault in Sydney’s east overnight.

At about 11pm on Saturday, emergency services responded to reports of an assault on Coogee Bay Road, Coogee.

A 26-year-old man was arrested at the scene and charged with assault occasioning actual bodily harm, NSW police said.

Paramedics treated a 41-year-old man at location before he was taken to Prince of Wales hospital, a NSW police statement said.

The 26-year-old man was refused bail to appear before the bail division court today.

A Jetstar pilot was forced to brake suddenly when a Qatar Airways plane came into “close proximity” while the other plane was taxiing at Sydney airport this morning.

Guardian Australia understands a Jetstar cabin crew member was injured in the incident, and was treated by paramedics.

The Jetstar flight from Sydney to the Gold Coast was taxiing out from its bay at Sydney airport this morning when the incident occurred.

double quotation markOur aircraft was following instructions by Air Traffic Control when the pilots were forced to brake firmly after another aircraft came in close proximity.
   We have commenced an investigation into the incident.

Coalition demands NDIS changes focus on fraud, corruption

Liberal frontbencher Tim Wilson also called on the government to focus more on fraud and corruption issues in the NDIS, as the Coalition and Labor negotiate on changes to the disability scheme.

The government’s bill is being examined by a parliamentary committee, with a report due this coming Friday. Labor may seek to bring that bill back on for debate and vote in the second week of this coming parliamentary sitting.

Wilson accused the government of “an ongoing tolerance” to fraud in the system. The NDIS minister, Jenny McAllister, was on News24 this morning also, and we’ll get you some of her contributions shortly.

double quotation markWe have people who are awarding either packages to people when they shouldn’t be used, we’re having people taking advantage of the system and we know this is being exposed.

And so as a consequence we’ve seen this massive growth continue to go on and we need to make sure that that’s the focus, not the targeting of the clients. You know, if you go out to voters in Australia, there are a lot of people who are on disability support packages who are very nervous about their future and it’s because of how this government has looked at reforms and they feel like they’re being targeted, not the fraudsters.

The shadow treasurer, Tim Wilson, says he’s concerned that gambling advertisers could still be able to reach children, under the government’s proposed wagering reforms.

Labor’s gambling bill has little support outside the government, with the Coalition, Greens and other cross benchers opposed. Amendments are being discussed to win support in the parliament, and while Wilson wouldn’t say which specific areas the Coalition was negotiating on, he said the bill may not go far enough to reduce harms for kids.

Speaking to News24 this morning, Wilson said:

double quotation markWe’re not wowsers, we do believe in protecting children, particularly from harm.

Under the government’s proposed bill, it doesn’t limit the capacity to advertise to children and that’s something that I’m concerned about, making sure that we’ve got the measures that are consistent, appropriate, and also reflecting the changing nature of technology

Wilson noted many people are watching sport on other platforms beyond TV. The proposed gambling rules include a quirk where streaming platforms will be able to show more ads during breaks in play, if those platforms offer a “triple lock” function which includes an opt-out feature.

“What we need to make sure is that the interests are in alignment, we’re protecting children and of course we’re making sure that measures are taken so that people aren’t taken advantage of,” Wilson said.

Victoria’s new premier, Ben Carroll, says the state government will boost its funding for public schools before the November election, and opening up a pathway for a federal cash injection.

In an interview with the ABC, Carroll pledged to increase funding of the state’s public schools by 5% – fulfilling its obligations under the former Gonski plan.

Victoria’s school funding model lags behind other jurisdictions, with the state only paying 70% of the Schooling Resource Standard – an estimate of a school’s funding based on student’s needs – and the federal government contributing 20%.

Under the national agreement, Carroll’s pledge means Canberra will match the funding increase to close the gap.

Carroll said he had discussed the funding increase with Anthony Albanese.

The teacher’s union has demanded the state fully fund public schools as part of its drawn-out pay dispute with the Victorian government.

ABC’s Insiders is marking its 25th birthday with a special anniversary edition this morning.

The show’s founding host, Barrie Cassidy, has returned to the couch for the first time since he retired in 2019.

Reflecting on how Australian politics has changed since the show began in 2001, Cassidy says:

double quotation markYou’ve had that degrading of the support for the major parties, 80% to 50% in the life of Insiders, and that’s quite extraordinary. It happened kind of like bankruptcy – slowly, and then all at once.

The all-at-once period was pretty much just in the lead-up to the last election.

(A reminder that you can hear more from Cassidy every week on the Guardian’s Back to Back Barries podcast.)

Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young was also asked about her call for a moratorium on building of data centres until there are the proper laws in place to regulate their impact on the country’ energy, water use, environment and communities.

Asked about the proposal, Hanson-Young said:

double quotation markI want an ironclad guarantee for the Australian people: their power bills won’t go up, their water is going to be protected, their jobs are going to be protected, and that they get some type of community benefit because without those things there is going to be no social license and it’s evaporating very quickly.

Hanson-Young says she had spoken to the communications minister, Anika Wells, about amendments to the government’s gambling reform but has not spoken directly to Anthony Albanese.

Asked if she expected to speak to the prime minister, the Greens senator said “I hope so”:

double quotation markThe government said they weren’t prepared to move at all, and now here they are. So, I mean … they’re playing games here.

Their own backbenchers know it’s not strong enough.

Hanson-Young said she would not vote for what was “on the table at the moment”

double quotation markIf you are not prepared to do what’s needed here, well, we’ll take this out of your hands and we’ll do it in the Senate ourselves.

Greens call on Albanese to put ‘cards on the table’ as gambling negotiations continue

Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young, has called for the Albanese government to put its “cards on the table” as part of a potential strengthening of its gambling reform.

Labor is expected to face strong opposition from gambling giants if it accedes to Coalition and Greens demands for a tough new ban on financial inducements for betting, as part of closely watched Senate deal making expected within days.

Speaking to the ABC’s Insiders, Hanson-Young said:

double quotation markIf the government’s now willing to move on some things … good. But the devil’s going to be in the detail. And what I say to the prime minister and to the government is, put your cards on the table.

SA premier meets Apple chief following social media ban

The premier of South Australia, Peter Malinauskas has visited Apple’s headquarters and met with outgoing chief executive Tim Cook in the United States.

Malinauskas posted on LinkedIn that Cook was keen to discuss the under-16s social media ban, which kicked off with South Australia’s proposal last year before the federal government adopted a national approach.

Apple has been keen to credit Australia with inspiring planned changes to parental controls on iPhones and iPads, with Cook calling the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, earlier this year when Apple announced the changes.

Documents released under freedom of information laws this week suggest the pair discussed the possibility of Albanese visiting Apple’s California headquarters on his next trip to the United States.

The documents surrounding the call between Albanese and Cook reveal an unnamed employee at Apple following up the call in late June and enquiring about “the possibility of the PM visiting Apple Park in Cupertino (California) when he visits the US for the UN General Assembly.”

Any potential visit by Albanese to Apple may come after Cook steps down as chief executive, and is replaced by John Ternus on 1 September, as the UN general assembly’s 81st session commences on 8 September.

New South Wales recorded its first cases of H5 bird flu in two local birds on Saturday, including one found near Wentworth on the Murray-Darling Basin.

Jack Gough, chief executive of the Invasive Species Council, said:

double quotation markThat should be ringing alarm bells for governments because it suggests it could soon be spreading among inland bird colonies ahead of spring breeding season.

Birds in the Murray-Darling basin are already in decline due to feral animals, insufficient water to critical wetlands and the loss of habitat - now they have a deadly disease to contend with.

Samples from two deceased greater crested terns in NSW – the other found near Narooma on the south coast – tested positive at CSIRO’s Australian Centre for Disease Preparedness.

On Saturday, a further 28 positive cases were confirmed in South Australia, bringing the state’s total to 147. An additional 13 suspected cases were also detected, including an ibis in Adelaide and a cormorant in Carpenter Rocks on the Limestone Coast.

Victoria confirmed 10 positive cases on Saturday, all from greater crested terns in south-west Victoria and Clyde in south-east Melbourne.

As of 3pm yesterday, Australia had a total of 215 H5 bird flu cases nationally.

This is Adeshola Ore here to take you through today’s news as it unfolds.

articles.title: Florida man allegedly kills family's kittens in front of teenage daughter as form of punishment: officials
articles.excerpt: Bodycam video shows Lee County deputies arresting a Fort Myers father accused of killing two family kittens and injuring a third as a form of punishment against his teenage daughter, according to auth...
articles.body_text:
Bodycam video shows Lee County deputies arresting a Fort Myers father accused of killing two family kittens and injuring a third as a form of punishment against his teenage daughter, according to authorities.

A Florida father was arrested this week for allegedly killing the family's kittens in front of his teenage daughter as a form of punishment, authorities said.

Bodycam video released by the Lee County Sheriff's Office shows deputies responding to a home in Pine Manor after receiving a report that a man was attempting to drown and strike a two-month-old kitten named Luna.

David Charette Jr., 48, was arrested and charged with aggravated animal cruelty after authorities accused him of killing two kittens and injuring a third.

Witnesses told deputies that Charette allegedly abused and killed the family's kittens in front of his teenage daughter as a form of punishment when she "acted up."

'DEEPLY DISTURBING' ANIMAL CRUELTY OPERATION INVOLVING BABY MONKEYS BUSTED BY ICE INVESTIGATION

Body camera footage shows David Charette Jr. speaking with Lee County deputies after authorities responded to allegations of animal cruelty at a home in Pine Manor, Fla. (Lee County Sheriff's Office)

Charette defended his treatment of Luna while speaking with deputies in the body camera video.

"The cat is in perfectly healthy condition," Charette told deputies. "I have to give the cat a bath because it soils itself in the cage."

"It's covered in crap and I have to give it a bath, and it cries, and she doesn't like that," he added.

Lee County Sheriff Carmine Marceno said the allegations involving Charette's daughter made the case particularly disturbing.

FLORIDA MAIL CARRIER ACCUSED OF SNATCHING PETS ON ROUTE, TRAPPING 100-PLUS CATS AND DOGS IN ‘HOARDING’ HOUSE

A 2-month-old kitten named Luna was taken to a local animal hospital for treatment and is recovering after an alleged animal cruelty incident, authorities said. (Lee County Sheriff's Office)

"A daughter says that when she acts up or when she's in trouble, her father kills her kittens. This is sickening to me," Marceno told CBS affiliate WINK.

Investigators said they later learned Charette had allegedly killed two other kittens over the previous year.

In June, Charette allegedly smothered a one-month-old kitten with a bleach-soaked rag, according to the sheriff's office.

In a separate incident, investigators said Charette allegedly killed a three-month-old kitten with a blow-dryer.

David Charette Jr., 48, was arrested and charged with aggravated animal cruelty after authorities accused him of killing two kittens and injuring a third. (Lee County Sheriff's Office)

Authorities said both kittens had been buried in the backyard, but investigators recovered only one during a search of the property.

Luna was taken to a local animal hospital for treatment and is recovering, according to the sheriff's office.

Michael Sinkewicz is a writer for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to michael.sinkewicz@fox.com

articles.title: UFC star Conor McGregor goes viral for drone delivery fiasco after undergoing knee surgery
articles.excerpt:
Megan Rapinoe's latest ridiculous rant on Sophie Cunningham and RIley Gaines makes it clear she doesn't get the real issues in women's sports

More and more things are becoming available via drone del...
articles.body_text:
Megan Rapinoe's latest ridiculous rant on Sophie Cunningham and RIley Gaines makes it clear she doesn't get the real issues in women's sports

More and more things are becoming available via drone delivery, and UFC star Conor McGregor just showed us all that there are still some kinks that need to be worked out with this system.

Last month at UFC 329, McGregor made his highly anticipated return to the octagon, which lasted 69 seconds due to an injury.

McGregor had surgery this week and decided to celebrate by getting an energy drink delivered to him by drone.

CONOR MCGREGOR HAS SURGERY ON TORN ACL, AGAIN VOWS COMEBACK: 'MY KNEE IS REPAIRED...THANK YOU GOD'

Conor McGregor's UFC return was short lived due to an injury, and he underwent surgery on his knee this week. (Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images)

The 38-year-old Irishman was spotted on a balcony trying to retrieve his beverage, which proved to be way more difficult than it probably should've been.

You'd think he'd have a guy who runs and gets him drinks, but hey, drone delivery is cool.

They recently started doing drone deliveries near where I live, and I've been hoping I forget something so I can try it.

DOORDASH GETS FAA APPROVAL FOR ITS OWN DELIVERY DRONES

However, McGregor's experience has me second-guessing it.

For starters, I don't think anyone has ever been happier to be on crutches than McGregor was when he realized that the sticks he's been hobbling around on could also be used as a makeshift arm extender. He's like a post-op Inspector Gadget.

But that proved to be easier said than done (though many pointed out that McGregor should've used the other end of the crutch so it could hook the drone tether).

It seems we have yet to hit the point in drone development when they can detect whether or not someone is swinging a crutch at them while trying to retrieve a can of energy drink. ((Photo by JOSH EDELSON / AFP)

What I don't get is why the drone just hovered there while an Irishman swung crutches at it.

Doesn't the drone have cameras or sensors to detect when someone is trying in vain to retrieve the payload?

It should. Then it could just move over a bit so someone like McGregor doesn't pop the stitches on that knee of his because he was trying to snag a Monster he had shipped by air and probably paid a premium for.

So, after seeing that display of McGregor demonstrating the shortcomings in drone delivery technology, I think I'll get groceries I forgot the old-fashioned way: by driving to the grocery store when my wife says we're out of something.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham speaks out against DiJonai Carrington after flagrant foul and 'White privilege' post
articles.excerpt:
Fox News contributor Kaylee McGhee White discusses backlash against Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham for her comments on women’s sports on ‘Outnumbered.’

Sophie Cunningham spoke out against Chica...
articles.body_text:
Fox News contributor Kaylee McGhee White discusses backlash against Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham for her comments on women’s sports on ‘Outnumbered.’

Sophie Cunningham spoke out against Chicago Sky star DiJonai Carrington after the Fever's 90-86 win on Saturday.

Carrington was ejected from the game in the first half after smacking Cunningham across the face during Cunningham's layup attempt.

Chicago Sky guard DiJonai Carrington commits a flagrant 2 foul against Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham. (Kamil Krzaczynski/Imagn Images)

"Clearly, I think it was like unnecessary. I've never really spoken to her and have no beef with her, but I guess she has some pent up stuff. So get your s--- off. That's fine. I can take it... Yeah, it's intentional," Cunningham said, per ESPN's Kareem Copeland on X.

DIJONAI CARRINGTON DECLARES 'WHITE PRIVILEGE' AFTER EJECTION FOR SMACKING SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM IN THE FACE

"She has no reason to be doing any of that. So good way to get her kicked out. I don't even know her. She wasn't even on the team last year when all that was going on. But I do think when people play the Fever, we're nationally televised, there's a lot of eyes on us and people just want attention. And that's her just trying to get attention."

After the foul, Cunningham and Carrington were seen getting in each other's faces and yelling, as referees had to separate them.

Sophie Cunningham confronts DiJonai Carrington after the latter committed a hard foul that led to her being ejected in the first quarter of Saturday's game between the Indiana Fever and the Chicago Sky. (Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images)

After Carrington's ejection, she went on Threads and wrote "White Privilege" and tagged the Indiana Fever. Cunningham rejected Carrington's suggestion that the ejection had anything to do with race.

"I think the league is taking care of that. This has nothing to do with race. Last year, I did the same thing and I got kicked out. And I deserved to be kicked out. There's no reason even to play that card," Cunningham added.

Meanwhile, Cunningham's own coach, Stephanie White, defended Carrington in the post-game press conference, while agreeing the flagrant foul and ejection was the right call.

"Yeah, I mean, look, it was a hard foul. I don't think that DiJonai intentionally came out to get her across the neck like she did. But it did happen and I thought it was the right call. But you know, one of the things about Nay is that she's gonna play her butt off, man. She's gonna compete. Nobody's gonna go walking in for a layup. And so, I don't oppose the hard foul. But I also don't think that she intentionally went for the neck," White said.

White declined to comment on Carrington's "White privilege" post.

White previously coached Carrington when both were with the Connecticut Sun in 2023-24. In the 2024 playoffs, Carrington poked Fever phenom Caitlin Clark in the eye.

Carrington's current coach, Sky coach Tyler Marsh, also defended Carrington and said he believed it wasn't a flagrant foul in the moment.

DiJonai Carrington of the Chicago Sky was ejected after a brutal foul on Sophie Cunningham of the Indiana Fever. (Kamil Krzaczynski/Imagn Images)

"In the moment, I thought that she made a play on a ball. I didn't think it warranted a flagrant 2, I didn't see it in the replay. So that was my initial thoughts," Marsh said. "I haven't looked at that play since, so I really don't know if it was justified or not."

Marsh also declined to comment on Carrington's "White privilege" post. He also rejected the notion that Carrington may have come into the game with more emotion to play against Cunningham due to Cunningham's recent public stance in support of protecting women's sports.

JD VANCE PRAISES SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM FOR 'SAVE WOMEN'S SPORTS' ACTIVISM

"I don't think there is ill intent on our end," he added.

Chicago Sky head coach Tyler Marsh called it a joke after Kamilla Cardoso took 15 shots without a single free throw, adding to growing frustration over WNBA officiating. (Getty Images)

The incident between the two players unfolded as Cunningham remained at the center of a widening political debate. Supporters held a fourth rally outside the venue of a Fever road game on Saturday, while counterprotesters also gathered near the United Center.

Cunningham has said she does not harbor hatred toward transgender people but believes protecting girls and women in sports is "common sense." White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt previously defended Cunningham, saying the backlash against her was "astonishing."

With another Cunningham rally already scheduled ahead of the Fever’s Aug. 22 game against the New York Liberty, controversy is bound to surround Cunningham and Indiana beyond Chicago.

Meanwhile, Carrington already had a contentious history with the Fever before Saturday. During the 2024 season, she mocked Caitlin Clark for what she believed was flopping and later called Indiana supporters "the nastiest fans in the W" after receiving racist abuse from some online users.

Carrington then struck Clark in the eye while defending a pass during the 2024 playoffs, leaving the Fever star with a black eye. Both players said the contact was accidental, although Carrington later drew renewed criticism after appearing to joke about the controversy during an Instagram Live video.

Carrington has also responded to accusations that she plays dirty, insisting she simply plays aggressively and always attempts to make a play on the ball. Beyond basketball, she has drawn attention for wearing an explicit anti-President Donald Trump sweatshirt and urging WNBA players to oppose Trump administration policies affecting women and the LGBTQ community.

Jackson Thompson is a sports reporter for Fox News Digital covering critical political and cultural issues in sports, with an investigative lens. Jackson's reporting has been cited in federal government actions related to the enforcement of Title IX, and in legacy media outlets including The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer, The Associated Press and ESPN.com.

articles.title: Hungary nominates former Supreme Court chief Andras Baka for presidency
articles.excerpt:
Hungary’s governing Tisza party has nominated Andras Baka, a former Supreme Court chief removed from his post by Viktor Orban’s government in 2012, as its candidate for the country’s presidency.

The ...
articles.body_text:
Hungary’s governing Tisza party has nominated Andras Baka, a former Supreme Court chief removed from his post by Viktor Orban’s government in 2012, as its candidate for the country’s presidency.

The nomination, announced Saturday by Prime Minister Peter Magyar, marks the latest step in Tisza’s effort to dismantle Orban’s influence over state institutions since the party’s landslide election victory in April ended his 16-year rule.

The decision to nominate Baka for the presidency comes weeks after Tisza used a constitutional amendment to remove Orban-era President Tamas Sulyok from office.

On Tuesday, Baka, 73, is expected to be elected by parliament, where Tisza holds a constitutional majority.

Magyar wrote on Facebook that the nomination, made by secret ballot within the party’s parliamentary group, was “one of its most important decisions so far”.

Tisza lawmakers said Baka had always “attached paramount importance to the principle of separation of powers, consistently standing up for the rule of law and judicial independence”, adding that his experience represented “a significant asset” as the party lays “the foundations for Hungary’s new constitutional order”.

Fidesz, the party now in opposition, said it would boycott the vote, accusing Tisza of authoritarian tactics – allegations it denies.

Baka served two terms as a judge on the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg before being elected head of Hungary’s Supreme Court in 2009.

He was removed two years later after publicly criticising Orban’s government reforms, which he said threatened judicial independence. The European court later ruled that his dismissal had violated his rights to a fair trial and freedom of expression, a judgement the Council of Europe said Hungary failed to fully implement.

Hungary’s presidency carries mostly ceremonial powers, with limited authority to veto or refer legislation, though the nomination is being treated as a heavily symbolic move.

articles.title: Scott Eastwood says his father sent Kevin Costner home from set while filming 'A Perfect World'
articles.excerpt:

articles.body_text:
The actor bought his dad a Silverado truck for Christmas once he found success as an actor.

Scott Eastwood is getting candid about how his father once asked a well-known actor to leave a movie set.

During a recent interview on the "Armchair Expert" podcast, the 40-year-old actor shared that everybody has "a lot of respect" for his father, Clint Eastwood, on set and that he "didn't raise his voice ever" while on set.

He then shared a "legendary story" about when his father worked with Kevin Costner, and how he reacted when the actor wouldn't leave his trailer, noting "I’m sort of going to paraphrase it, and I’ll probably tell it a little wrong."

"Kevin Costner sort of going through maybe, the Kevin Costner rise to fame and maybe got a big ego, you know, blah blah blah, but they were doing 'Perfect World,'" he said. "Apparently, he didn't want to come out of his trailer for some reason."

Scott Eastwood said his dad never raised his voice while on set. (Aitor Rosas Sune/WWD via Getty Images)

GOLDIE HAWN SOUNDS THE ALARM ON CHILDHOOD CELEBRITY CULTURE: 'ALL I CAN SAY IS IT'S A NIGHTMARE'

Scott said Clint — who directed and starred in the film — reacted by saying, "Well send him home then," even though Costner was scheduled to be in the scene they were working on that day.

"So he sent him home, and I guess they just went to Kevin and said, 'Hey, you're going to go home for the day,'" Scott explained. "He said, 'What do you mean I'm in the scene?' You know, 'Well, I guess you're not anymore. Clint changed that.'"

After he was asked to leave the set that day, Scott noted, "I think the next day he was on set ready to go."

Fox News Digital reached out to representatives for Costner for comment.

Scott Eastwood said his dad once asked Kevin Costner to leave a movie set because he wouldn't come out of his trailer. (Getty Images)

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"A Perfect World" stars Costner as an escaped convict who kidnaps a young child, with Clint playing the role of a Texas ranger who is searching for Costner and the young boy.

Scott previously discussed how growing up with a famous father impacted his work ethic and how he conducts himself on set, noting that growing up he saw "some behavior in this business that is shocking."

"I think I was lucky in some ways because I got to see it growing up and got to see like how it's bulls---," he said on an episode of "The Joe Rogan Experience," in June of certain behaviors on modern movie sets.

While Eastwood said he got a peek at bad behavior on set when he was younger and visiting his iconic dad on set, the "Wrath of Man" star said his father "did a really good job of protecting" him and his siblings from the pitfalls that come with child stardom.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Scott credits growing up on film sets with his dad for opening his eyes to what is and isn't acceptable behavior on set. (E. Charbonneau/WireImage for Lionsgate)

He brought it up after he and Rogan began talking about child stars who found fame at a really young age, saying, "you get stunted in your growth" when you get famous too young.

"I mean, kudos to my dad, [be]cause he did a really good job of protecting us from that and very private," he said. "We didn't live in LA, we lived in Carmel. It was a very...as normal as it could be, in the sense that he was like, 'No, you just you need to be a normal child and learn how the world works.'"

Lori A. Bashian is an entertainment news writer at Fox News Digital.

LIV Golf is hosting its New York event at President Donald Trump’s National Golf Club Bedminster.

It's the third time that the upstart tour has held an event at one of the president's golf clubs.

As was the case at one previous event, President Trump himself was on hand to check things out.

TRUMP DRAWS MUCH DIFFERENT REACTION AT NBA FINALS THAN HE DID AT CFP NATIONAL TITLE GAME

President Donald Trump drives a golf cart at a LIV Golf event at his Trump National Golf Club Bedminster in New Jersey. (Dennis Schneidler-Imagn Images)

According to The New York Post, the commander-in-chief received a big ovation from spectators as he drove a golf cart along the course.

It's always interesting to hear how Trump is received at various sporting events, but you can usually make a pretty good guess.

So, I think it would've been kind of odd if he had been greeted with anything other than cheers at his own golf club.

Trump National Golf Club in Bedminster, New Jersey hosted the LIV Golf New York event. (Photo by Andrew Mordzynski/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Of course, the president being on hand for this weekend's event is a big deal for LIV Golf, which is going through an interesting time at the moment.
