Hunter Biden has told the BBC he is "the most privileged person there is" after receiving a presidential pard...
articles.body_text:
Watch: Hunter Biden says pardon was 'not good' for his father's legacy or American people

Hunter Biden has told the BBC he is "the most privileged person there is" after receiving a presidential pardon from his father, former US President Joe Biden, acknowledging it was not a good choice for America or his father's legacy.

In a wide-ranging interview with the BBC's Newsnight, Hunter Biden defended the controversial pardon, revealed his father's "painful" cancer has spread, ruled out seeking elected office and spoke about helping others recover from addiction.

Asked about the 2024 pardon, he said he understood the criticism but noted: "What would you have thought of my dad if he did not do that for me."

"It's something that is easily criticised and for good reason," he added.

"It's not fair… All I know is that I'm grateful that he did it for me," he said, acknowledging the pardon was "not good" for the American people, the Constitution - or his father's legacy.

He argued to the BBC that his father ultimately acted out of concern that he would become a target under Donald Trump's incoming administration.

"I was the only one in the world that could have gotten what I got from the only person in the world who could give it, my father."

Hunter Biden also insisted he and his father had never discussed the possibility of a pardon before it was granted.

"There is no way that you can have those kinds of discussions that would not become public," he said.

President Biden granted his son a full and unconditional pardon in December 2024, despite repeatedly saying beforehand that he would not use the powers of the presidency to intervene in his son's legal cases. In announcing the decision, the former president said his son had been "selectively and unfairly prosecuted".

The pardon covered his son's federal gun conviction, a tax case he'd pled guilty to and any federal offences committed between 2014 and 2024.

'It's really, really hard' - Hunter Biden gets emotional about his father's cancer battle

Asked about the depths of his addiction, he described drinking almost a gallon of vodka a day while smoking crack cocaine almost every 15 minutes at its worst.

"It was hell on earth," he said. "There's nothing glamorous about it."

Reflecting on why he turned to drugs and alcohol, Hunter Biden rejected the suggestion that he felt untouchable because he was the son of a president.

"I wasn't reaching for anything except oblivion," he said. He noted that his addiction was a way to escape feelings of anxiety and isolation.

The drugs and alcohol initially felt like a solution before becoming "the thing that almost killed me", he noted.

Hunter Biden got emotional at times in the interview, notably when discussing his father's health.

Cancer is really hard," he said, stopping to clear his throat. "It's really sad to watch."

He revealed that the "cancer has spread, metastasised into his bones and further. It's very painful" and "very debilitating".

"My dad is, to this day, the centre of our family," he said. "He's the best father, the best husband, the best grandfather."

"The only thing that I say about my dad, about his health right now, is I wish he would complain more."

Hunter Biden also reflected on the presidential debate in June 2024 that ultimately ended his father's re-election campaign. He said he had watched it from his home in California and immediately sensed something was wrong.

"I was shocked," he said. "I knew something was wrong."

Hunter Biden tells BBC pardon was 'not good' for his father's legacy or American people

Hunter Biden has previously argued that his father's poor debate performance reflected physical exhaustion after extensive travel. Following Joe Biden's cancer diagnosis, he has also questioned whether the illness may already have been affecting his father.

He said his father remains politically engaged and determined to continue speaking publicly.

When asked about rumours that he might enter politics - or even make a run for the presidency - Biden said he himself had "no interest in elected politics" and dismissed any suggestion that he would one day seek office.

Instead, Biden said he wanted to devote his time to speaking about addiction and recovery, which he described as a cause capable of bridging America's political divides.

"I believe that addiction and the hope of recovery are something that connect us all," he said.

Asked what made him proudest of his father, Hunter Biden pointed not to his years in public office but to his resilience.

"I'm most proud of his resilience," he said. "He's proven time and time again that when you get knocked down, you can get up.

Melania Trump threatens to sue Hunter Biden for $1bn over Epstein claim

Hunter Biden lashes out at George Clooney over father's 2024 election exit

Hunter Biden says he can't afford to continue laptop-related lawsuit

articles.title: The Pittsburgh Penguins may have just given out one of the riskiest contracts in NHL history
articles.excerpt:
Megan Rapinoe's latest ridiculous rant on Sophie Cunningham and RIley Gaines makes it clear she doesn't get the real issues in women's sports

There have been a lot of interesting signings this NHL of...
articles.body_text:
Megan Rapinoe's latest ridiculous rant on Sophie Cunningham and RIley Gaines makes it clear she doesn't get the real issues in women's sports

There have been a lot of interesting signings this NHL offseason, with the Flyers forcing the Ducks to pay top dollar for Leo Carlsson, Patrick Kane signing a nice deal to return to the Blackhawks and Macklin Celebrini getting the big money from the San Jose Sharks.

But the most intriguing deal may have come from the Pittsburgh Penguins, who signed a player with just 47 career games to an eight-year, $32 million deal after he registered 7 points (2G, 5A) in 39 games last season.

Reread those numbers if you need to, but your eyes did not deceive you. That's the deal Penguins GM Kyle Dubas gave Finnish forward Ville Koivunen on Thursday.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Now, first of all, this is awesome for Koivunen. But Dubas may as well be wearing a stars-and-stripes jumpsuit, because this deal has an Evel Knievel-level risk.

That's because while the salary cap and therefore player contracts are going up, paying a player with that kind of production an AAV of $4 million is a massive gamble.

Sure, the numbers come from a small sample, but they're still not blowing any minds.

Still, the Penguins like what they see enough to keep him around long-term.

Penguins forward Ville Koivunen has played parts of two season with the team, but it was enough to earn him a big 8-year, $32 million deal. (Photo by Joe Sargent/NHLI via Getty Images)

That could be because his AHL numbers with the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins the last two seasons have been pretty great. Just last year, he posted 41 points (13G, 28A) in just 34 games. Before that, he was really solid playing in SM-liiga in his native Finland too.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON’T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Is solid production in the AHL and abroad, but so-so results in the NHL now worth a long-term deal at $4 million per year?

But who knows? If Koivunen clicks, it may soon turn out to be a very team-friendly deal.

While he has had some trouble getting on NHL scoresheets, Koivunrn has played well in the American Hockey League the last two seasons. (Photo by Joe Sargent/NHLI via Getty Images))

The one thing to remember is that the team may only have a few more years of paying its current core veterans like Evgeni Malkin, Kris Letang and Sidney Crosby, who has a famously team-friendly $8.7 million AAV deal.

But if Koivunen's production doesn't ramp up, good luck finding a trading partner willing to take that deal off your hands.

articles.title: Spain to introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy
articles.excerpt:
Move comes in response to Rome imposing similar measures after mass migration rush to Ceuta

Spain has announced it will introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy in response to Rome im...
articles.body_text:
Move comes in response to Rome imposing similar measures after mass migration rush to Ceuta

Spain has announced it will introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass rush of people from Morocco into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until 7 September, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

Hours earlier, Spain threatened Italy with countermeasures if it did not swiftly lift its own border checks, drawing a rebuff from Rome.

The rare spat between the EU and Nato allies came after tens of thousands of people crossed from Morocco to Spain’s north African territory on 30-31 July in an unprecedented, deadly rush.

The scenes infuriated EU members that back a hard line on irregular immigration, including Italy, which imposed border checks on people arriving from Spain for one month.

The Spanish government criticised the measure on Friday as “unfair, contrary to the EU’s interests and discriminatory for the Spanish population”.

Foreign minister José Manuel Albares described it as “a torpedo fired at the hull of European unity”.

“We urge the government of Italy to rectify, put an end to the checks and treat Spaniards like other European citizens,” he added.

He threatened “proportional measures” in response by Sunday if Italy failed to comply.

Within hours, the government of Italy’s far-right prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, said it “had no intention of revising the decision” before 15 August, when it said Spanish authorities “expected a new wave of migration” to hit Ceuta.

Meloni’s office said in a statement: “Italy does not accept ultimatums or impositions from abroad regarding national security and border control.

“Only when there is certainty that there are no security or terrorism risks to Italy, that no new wave is occurring, and that no irregular migrants are heading toward European territory, will the decision be reconsidered.”

Spain’s interior ministry announced the reciprocal measures within hours.

Spanish police have been monitoring online rumours and social media about possible fresh arrivals in Ceuta in mid-August, according to local media. But authorities have not expressly said they expect a repeat of last week’s rush.

Border authorities would in the meantime “do their utmost to ensure maximum ease of movement for Spanish and European citizens” who are not affected by border checks, the Italian statement added.

Italy, which does not share a land border with Spain, introduced border controls at maritime and air entry points for third-country nationals arriving from Spain.

The move, announced on 31 July, was an “extraordinary measure” intended to “safeguard national security and prevent possible repercussions for our nation”, Meloni said at the time.

She was among several EU leaders who called for Spain to be suspended from the visa-free Schengen travel zone after the Ceuta incident, despite such a move being legally impossible.

Italy’s coalition government has sought to stop the tens of thousands of people who land in small boats on the country’s shores each year.

The Spanish government warned against “creating rifts and sterile conflicts driven by internal electoral motives” and said “we trust that pro-European sentiment, common sense and good faith prevail”.

Of the 72,000 people who entered Ceuta, 70,000 have returned to Morocco, according to official Spanish figures.

Spanish authorities said 80 people died in the crossings.

Moroccan rights groups, however, estimate the figure to be higher. The Moroccan Association for Human Rights and the European Coordination for Human Rights in Morocco on Friday said at least 141 deaths were recorded and that the toll was likely to rise.

Morocco’s interior ministry has said 11 people died on its side of the border, all but one by drowning.

Those who remain in Ceuta – including hundreds of unaccompanied children – face dire living conditions with little access to food, water and shelter.

articles.title: Former first lady Jill Biden doubts she'll see a woman president in her lifetime
articles.excerpt:
Former first lady Jill Biden lamented on "The View" about how some famous Democrats, even friends her and former President Joe Biden had known for decades, turned against him after his 2024 debate.

F...
articles.body_text:
Former first lady Jill Biden lamented on "The View" about how some famous Democrats, even friends her and former President Joe Biden had known for decades, turned against him after his 2024 debate.

Former first lady Jill Biden doubted she would see a female president in her lifetime on Wednesday, and said she was sure it was going to be former Vice President Kamala Harris.

During a conversation on Kelly Ripa's "Let's Talk Off Camera" podcast, Ripa asked the former first lady if she felt they would see a female president in their lifetimes.

"In my lifetime? Well, I'm 75. So, you know, I feel like probably not in my lifetime, Kelly, but maybe in yours," she responded.

KAMALA HARRIS IS THE 'FAIRLY OBVIOUS' 2028 PRESIDENTIAL FRONTRUNNER, DEMOCRATIC INSIDERS SAY

Biden said she was confident Harris would be the first woman president.

Former first lady Jill Biden as a guest on "The View" airing Tuesday, June 2, 2026. (ABC via Getty Images)

"But I really did think last time that Kamala was going to win. I mean, I was out on the campaign trail for her. I saw the excitement," Biden said. "I saw the crowds. I saw, you know, at the convention. I mean, I saw all the energy and I thought, finally, we're going to have a woman president."

Patrice Onwuka, the Vice President of economic policy at Independent Women, told Fox News Digital in a statement that the ex-first lady's comments were a slap in the face.

"Jill Biden’s comments about never expecting to see a female president is a slap to the bench of female Democrats that have 2028 aspirations, like AOC and Gretchen Whitmer. The supposed party of women can’t even convince the former First Lady of its prospects to elect a woman at the top of the ticket," Onwuka said.

DEMOCRATS’ MIDTERM PUSH CLOUDED BY INFIGHTING OVER PARTY KEEPING 2024 AUTOPSY UNDER WRAPS

Onwuka told Fox News Digital Harris' loss was about her being a status quo candidate.

Kelly Ripa attends the 79th Annual Tony Awards at Radio City Music Hall on June 7, 2026, in New York City. (Dia Dipasupil/WireImage)

"Kamala Harris blew a billion-dollar campaign chest and a coronation on the top of the presidential ticket to only lose. Perhaps it’s time to stop fixating on gender and take policy seriously. Democrats failed to make Americans’ lives better in 2024. They didn’t care about a first female president if she was just going to continue the status quo. This fate lays wait for any female candidate who cannot deliver economic mobility for regular Americans," she added.

Ripa said during the conversation she was "less hopeful" than the former first lady.

"I'm hoping that at a certain point, that that turns around. I don't know what it's going to take. I don't think social media helps," Ripa added. "I will always keep moving forward. I just, you know, I just feel like there has to be something internally. There's got to be a messenger eventually that breaks through the people."

MICHELLE OBAMA SAYS AMERICA GOING THROUGH ITS 'JANKY' ERA

Former first lady Michelle Obama has also said she didn't believe the U.S. was ready for a female president.

In November, Obama told a crowd that America "ain’t ready" to elect a woman, pointing to Harris’s loss to President Donald Trump in 2024.

Harris pushed back on the notion in December 2025.

"I do believe the country is ready," Harris told The New York Times at the time.

MICHELLE OBAMA ACCUSES MEDIA OF WEAPONIZING FASHION TO 'DIMINISH' HER AS A CAMPAIGN THREAT

"Thousands of people are coming to hear my voice. Thousands and thousands," Harris said in the interview, referring to her book tour. "Every place we’ve gone has been sold out."

Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi also pushed back on Obama's remarks, but said the U.S. still needed to change.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

When asked by CNN's Anderson Cooper whether she agreed with the former first lady's comments, Pelosi questioned why a woman commander-in-chief would be out of the question.

"Well, I hope — I mean, I respect her and I know that view is one that we all are saddened by, but we — I think we have to change. The fact is that I‘ve heard every excuse in the book, you know, like, 'I‘m not sure a woman could be commander-in-chief.' Well, why not?" she asked. "'Well, I served in the military.' Well, OK. And so? So do women serve in the military."

Hanna Panreck is an associate editor at Fox News.

articles.title: Idaho police release video of In-N-Out Burger mass shooting that killed three
articles.excerpt:
Officials praise unarmed employee from nearby store for engaging 24-year-old gunman who later killed himself

Police released video on Friday of a mass shooting that killed three people at an Idaho In...
articles.body_text:
Officials praise unarmed employee from nearby store for engaging 24-year-old gunman who later killed himself

Police released video on Friday of a mass shooting that killed three people at an Idaho In-N-Out Burger restaurant last weekend, and praised an unarmed employee from a nearby store who engaged the gunman outdoors, slowing him down and possibly preventing more deaths as authorities were catching up.

The video released by the police also showed at least three people confronted the gunman with their own weapons during the incident.

“What happened here was violent, frightening and deeply traumatic,” the Twin Falls police chief, Matthew Hicks, said during a news conference before screening an eight-and-a-half minute compilation of surveillance camera and bodycam video of the incident.

The distressing video, which was edited by the police to blur faces and omit graphic images, revealed more details of the chaotic scene last weekend. It shows that the gunman walked up to the drive-thru window four times and opened fire, killing an In-N-Out employee, police said.

Ten people were shot – inside the restaurant, directly outside, on an adjacent busy road and at a car charging station in a Twin Falls visitor center lot, Hicks said.

Hicks said investigators still do noty have a motive for the shooting. The gunman, identified as Chad Williams, 24, killed himself when police officers caught up to him on a nearby walking trail.

It should have been a “normal Saturday afternoon”, Hicks said at the televised news conference. “Employees showing up for work. Visitors coming to see our beautiful city. Instead they were confronted with chaos, fear and now loss.”

As the shooting unfolded, employees from nearby stores fled to a walking trail. When the gunman headed to the trail, he came across two people, including one with his hands in the air who spoke to him, the video shows.

That man distracted the gunman from possibly pursuing others on the trail. Williams subsequently killed himself as police closed in. His body was found near a canyon.

“To that young man, you are a hero,” Hicks said of the bystander who slowed the gunman down. “Your courage, your composure, your selflessness in that moment likely gave others the time they needed to escape harm. This community is grateful for you, and we will never forget what you did that day.”

Hicks also praised the work of an off-duty state trooper, who shot at Williams from inside the restaurant, and a former police officer, AJ James, who was wounded while confronting him.

Authorities had previously credited an armed civilian who fired back and diverted Williams from the restaurant.

James ran toward the sound of gunfire from the drive-thru window, while the off-duty officer inside the In-N-Out exchanged gunfire with Williams through the window and directed workers out of the building, Hicks said.

He acted “heroically and unbelievably” to try to slow down the shooter, the police chief said, declining to release the off-duty officer’s name.

Braxton Steube said he was the person who encountered Williams on the trail after fleeing a Dick’s Sporting Good store.

“I said, ‘I have a family.’ I said, ‘You don’t have to do this. I’ll tell you whatever you want. I’ll do anything,’” Steube told KMVT-TV in Twin Falls.

“He started to like tear up a bit, it seemed. And he said to me, ‘Just get away from me, man.’”

Steube said the gunman shot at him and missed.

Police identified those killed as Ashley Garibay, 23, of Stockton, California; Dale Schultz, 66, of Salt Lake City; and Christopher Claunch, 59, of Hagerman, Idaho.

Williams had briefly attended the College of Southern Idaho and previously lived in Arizona.

articles.title: Prosecutor fired over blogposts critical of Trump sues US justice department
articles.excerpt:
Will Rosenzweig’s defunct blog was publicized online by conservative pundit who tagged senior DoJ officials

A federal prosecutor fired last year over critical comments he had written as a private cit...
articles.body_text:
Will Rosenzweig’s defunct blog was publicized online by conservative pundit who tagged senior DoJ officials

A federal prosecutor fired last year over critical comments he had written as a private citizen about Donald Trump sued the justice department on Friday, saying his termination violated his first amendment rights.

Will Rosenzweig was two weeks away from trying a multimillion-dollar Medicare fraud case when a blog he had written years earlier covering a broad range of topics was publicized online by a conservative political commentator who also included a screenshot of Rosenzweig’s LinkedIn account and tagged senior justice department officials for their awareness.

Less than three hours after the post, the lawsuit says, Rosenzweig received an email signed by then attorney general Pam Bondi informing him that he had been fired. The news came as Rosenzweig was out of town with his family observing the Jewish holiday of Rosh Hashana.

The September 2025 termination was part of a sweeping personnel purge over the last year and a half inside the justice department, which has fired prosecutors who worked on investigations into Trump and others seen as being against the administration’s efforts.

A lawsuit filed in federal court in Miami, where Rosenzweig worked as a federal prosecutor for five years, seeks reinstatement to the job as well as backpay and a court order declaring his firing unlawful.

The complaint says Rosenzweig was a highly respected prosecutor who received “consistent praise and awards” and was so highly valued in his office that he was told just weeks before his firing that he would be getting a special parking spot due to his performance.

“Will Rosenzweig was an excellent prosecutor who returned millions of dollars to the taxpayers by prosecuting healthcare fraud cases,” said a statement from his lawyers, Margaret Donovan, Daniel Fridman and Adam Fels.

“Yet the Department of Justice fired him on the eve of trial because, years ago as a private citizen, he published criticisms of President Trump. Since the current Department of Justice will not stand up for the first amendment and the American people, we will. We look forward to vindicating Will’s rights in court.”

The blog Rosenzweig had maintained had been defunct for over six years at the time of his firing and included his thoughts on travel, sports and other “apolitical, anodyne topics” in addition to critical observations about Trump and other political candidates, the lawsuit says.

The conservative commentator, Natalie Winters, who has a large online following, characterized Rosenzweig as “a rogue Trump hater” as she posted screenshots of some of his political musings, according to the complaint, which characterizes the firing as a direct assault on Rosenzweig’s free-speech rights.

“The department’s conduct rests on a single premise: a citizen must forever refrain from criticizing the government and its leaders to remain eligible to serve it,” the lawsuit says.

“That rule would force every American who might one day serve to choose between speaking freely now and working for the government later. Conditioning public employment on political loyalty, where a party card rather than merit opens the door to a government job, is a way of life in Havana and Caracas. It has no place here.”

A justice department spokeswoman declined to comment, citing pending litigation.

Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Earth, Wind & Fire canceled plans to take the stage Thursday evening in San Francisco after a medical emergency involving one of the band’s members.

The legendary group announced the unexpected change shortly before its scheduled performance Thursday at the Chase Center.

"We are unable to perform as scheduled tonight at Chase Center in San Francisco due to a medical emergency involving a member of our band," a statement posted on the band's social media account said.

"As a result, tonight’s show with Lionel Richie will be rescheduled, with a new date to be announced soon.

BARRY MANILOW RESCHEDULES CONCERT 45 MINUTES BEFORE START AMID ONGOING LUNG CANCER RECOVERY

Earth, Wind & Fire abruptly canceled a concert Aug. 6 due to a medical emergency. The show with Lionel Richie will be rescheduled. (Medios y Media/Getty Images)

"Ticket holders should retain their tickets, which will be honored for the new date, or refunds will be available at the point of purchase," the statement continued. "We sincerely apologize for the unexpected change and appreciate everyone’s understanding."

No additional details about the nature of the medical emergency were immediately provided.

Philip Bailey, Lionel Richie, Ralph Johnson and Verdine White of Earth, Wind & Fire backstage during the opening night of Sing A Song All Night Long. (Adam Bettcher/Getty Images for Live Nation)

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

R&B group Earth, Wind & Fire pose for a studio portrait during the mid-1970s. (Michael Ochs Archives/Getty Images)

Fox News Digital reached out to the band's representatives for additional comment.

Earth, Wind & Fire joined Richie for the Sing A Song All Night Long Tour beginning in June. The group made stops across North America, including Canada, and had just begun a California leg.

Founder Maurice White established the band in Chicago around 1969.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Verdine White, Philip Bailey and Ralph Johnson of Earth, Wind & Fire perform onstage during the 2026 Tribeca Festival. (Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images for Tribeca Festival)

Key members through the classic era included his brother Verdine White, Philip Bailey, Ralph Johnson, Larry Dunn, Al McKay, Fred White, Andrew Woolfolk and others.

articles.title: Chicago Sky address Sophie Cunningham rally planned outside home game vs Fever
articles.excerpt: Michele Tafoya joins the program and calls Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham a HERO for standing up for women's sports despite intense backlash from Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve, Seattle Storm...
articles.body_text:
Michele Tafoya joins the program and calls Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham a HERO for standing up for women's sports despite intense backlash from Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve, Seattle Storm leadership, and activist critics.

The Chicago Sky have addressed the upcoming Sophie Cunningham rally set to take place outside the United Center on Saturday ahead of the Sky's game against the Indiana Fever.

"The Chicago Sky are committed to providing a welcoming space for all, and we remain focused on basketball and offering fans a great experience at the United Center. As always, we expect that everyone will continue to follow all standard arena safety, security, media and fan code-of-conduct policies and protocols," read a statement provided to Fox News Digital.

Sophie Cunningham #8 of the Indiana Fever looks on against the Minnesota Lynx in the fourth quarter at Target Center on August 02, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Lynx defeated the Fever 108-100. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) (David Berding/Getty Images)

Saturday's game will see the fourth rally in support of Cunningham after she publicly came out in support of protecting women's sports from biological males, in an ESPN article that published last month.

WHITE HOUSE DEFENDS WNBA STAR SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM AFTER SHE SPEAKS OUT IN SUPPORT OF PROTECTING WOMEN'S SPORTS

Rallies have already taken place ahead of Fever games in Seattle, Portland and Minneapolis, and a fifth is already scheduled to take place in New York ahead of the Fever's game against the Liberty on Aug. 22.

Riley Gaines and Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham pose for a photo following Sunday's game at Target Center against the Minnesota Lynx. (Riley Gaines/XX-XY Athletics)

The WNBA has seen a surge in attention around the issue of biological males in women's sports in recent weeks, as four head coaches have come under scrutiny after sharing their thoughts on the subject, while former NBA player Enes Kanter-Freedom announced Friday he is declaring to play in the WNBA.

FORMER NBA FIRST ROUND PICK ENES KANTER FREEDOM DECLARES FOR 2027 WNBA DRAFT

The Cunningham rallies helped ignite that growth in awareness, as they have turned Fever road games into recurring flashpoints in the debate over transgender participation in women’s sports. The Seattle stop resulted in discipline for Storm co-owner Celeste Keaton after two teenage Cunningham supporters alleged that she cursed at them courtside.

Jennifer Sey posing with a Sophie Cunningham poster. (XX-XY Athletics)

Saturday’s rally will bring that debate to another major WNBA market, and the planned New York demonstration signals it will not end in Chicago.

Jackson Thompson is a sports reporter for Fox News Digital covering critical political and cultural issues in sports, with an investigative lens. Jackson's reporting has been cited in federal government actions related to the enforcement of Title IX, and in legacy media outlets including The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer, The Associated Press and ESPN.com.

articles.title: San Francisco dad questioned by park rangers for teaching his own kids tennis at public court
articles.excerpt:
Sam Dogen says he was warned he could face a $192 fine for teaching tennis without a permit at a San Francisco park, where he was practicing with his young children.

A California father says he simpl...
articles.body_text:
Sam Dogen says he was warned he could face a $192 fine for teaching tennis without a permit at a San Francisco park, where he was practicing with his young children.

A California father says he simply wanted to spend an afternoon playing tennis with his children but instead found himself being questioned by park rangers who believed he was illegally teaching lessons without a permit.

Sam Dogen, a San Francisco father of two, told Fox News Digital he was practicing with his 6-year-old daughter and 9-year-old son at Golden Gate Heights Park after returning from a family trip to Hawaii.

"I took the kids out for what I thought would be a nice afternoon ... to get over the jet lag, be outside in the sun and go play some tennis like we've done many, many times," Dogen said.

About 20 minutes into their practice session, Dogen said two San Francisco Recreation and Parks Department rangers approached and asked whether he had a permit to teach tennis.

CANNABIS CAFES MAY BECOME TOURIST DRAW IN US CITY AS LUNG EXPERTS CITE 'TOXIC CHEMICAL' CONCERNS

A San Francisco dad says he was playing tennis with his kids at Golden Gate Heights Park when he was approached by city park rangers. (Yalonda M. James/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images, File)

"I was immediately thinking to myself, 'What are you talking about? These are my kids,'" he recalled.

According to Dogen, the confusion ended only after one of his children spoke up.

"He's my daddy," his son told the rangers, Dogen said.

The family was never cited, but Dogen said one ranger told him the penalty for teaching without a permit could have been $192.

MODERATE SAN FRANCISCO MAYOR'S 'POLITICAL MACHINE' INDICATES THE CITY'S SHIFT TO THE CENTER: REPORT

Sam Dogen speaks with Fox News Digital during a video interview about his encounter with San Francisco park rangers. (Brittany Miller/Fox News Digital)

Dogen emphasized that the encounter ended with what he described as an educational warning, not a citation. Still, he questioned why the interaction happened at all.

"There was nobody waiting," he said. "It was just a surprise to me. Why even bother trying to disrupt a perfectly nice afternoon, father with his children?"

The Recreation and Parks Department previously told The San Francisco Standard that rangers routinely check whether people providing instruction on public courts are operating commercially, since paid tennis instruction requires a permit.

"This was a routine interaction," department spokesperson Tamara Aparton told the outlet. "Because paid instruction is not allowed on public courts without a permit, rangers will sometimes ask questions to determine whether someone is providing commercial instruction or simply using the courts for personal recreation or coaching their kids."

SAN FRANCISCO JUDGE NOT CONVINCED REPARATIONS FUND WILL BE DISCRIMINATORY DURING LAWSUIT HEARING

The San Francisco Recreation and Parks Department routinely checks whether people providing instruction on public tennis courts are operating commercially. (Smith Collection/Gado/Getty Images, File)

Dogen said he understands why the city regulates commercial instruction but added that he believes parents teaching their own children should be treated differently.

"Raising children in a city as expensive as San Francisco is hard enough," Dogen told Fox News Digital. "When you add law enforcement officers who aren't friendly, it gets even tougher."

He said his immediate concern during the interaction was making sure the situation stayed calm with his children standing nearby.

"My only instinct was to de-escalate and keep my 6-year-old daughter and 9-year-old son safe," Dogen said.

Looking ahead, Dogen joked that he may carry documentation with him the next time he takes his children to the public courts.

A family's game of tennis came under scrutiny by San Francisco park officials. (David Gray/Getty Images, File)

"I'm going to get their birth certificates and carry them with me in my tennis bag just to prove they're my children," he said. "I'm not going to get a permit to teach my children."

Dogen said he hopes the incident prompts city officials to take a more family-friendly approach to enforcing park rules.

"My hope is that San Francisco becomes a more welcoming place for children and families, not a place where a father teaching his own kids tennis on an empty court gets threatened with a $192 fine," he said.

Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

articles.title: Thai PM vows to introduce stricter gun laws after eight killed in shooting
articles.excerpt:
Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has pledged to introduce stricter gun laws

Thailand's prime minister has vowed to introduce new gun control laws in the wake of a shooting by a teenager on the...
articles.body_text:
Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has pledged to introduce stricter gun laws

Thailand's prime minister has vowed to introduce new gun control laws in the wake of a shooting by a teenager on the outskirts of Bangkok that left eight people dead and 22 injured.

The 14-year-old killed his grandparents at the home they shared, before travelling to Debsirin School in Nonthaburi, where he was a student. There, he killed five teachers before taking his own life. Later, Thai media reported that a student had also died from their injuries.

Speaking after the attack, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said he plans to introduce laws that restrict the carrying of firearms in public, with the new legislation only allowing government officials on duty to carry guns.

I was standing in front of my teacher when she was shot, Thai pupil says

Police Colonel Thadsakorn Konthong said that the gun and bullets used in the attack belonged to the teen's grandfather, with an initial inspection finding signs that the firearm had been searched for inside the grandfather's bedroom.

International and local media have reported that the gun was legally registered and had a permit.

Thailand has one of the highest rates of civilian gun ownership in South East Asia, with around 10.3 million firearms in civilian possession, around four million of which are believed to be owned illegally.

The country has strict gun laws, which punish the illegal possession of arms with up to 10 years in jail, but enforcement of these laws has been an issue.

During his time as interior minister, Anutin introduced a number of gun control laws, including a short-term ban on new gun licenses and import restrictions.

Speaking on Friday, the prime minister said the tragedy "shouldn't have happened".

"I don't just feel sorry for the victims but I feel sorry that this happened. How can this happen in our country," Anutin added.

The teenager is believed to have shot his 73-year-old grandfather and 74-year-old grandmother at their two-storey flat at around 05:00 local time on Friday (22:00 GMT on Thursday).

Each was killed by a single shot to the head, a Thai police official said.

After killing his grandparents, the teenager boarded a school bus carrying the firearm and dozens of bullets, Reuters news agency reported.

He then attended his first class at 08:30 and his second at 09:20.

Police have been combing over the school for evidence

Around half an hour into his second class of the day, he drew the gun and began shooting.

The teenager is believed to have first shot teachers on the school's sixth floor, killing three of them.

"He then walked down the stairs and encountered the school's deputy director and the director's secretary, who were going up the stairs to check on the situation," Police Major General Dejrapee Kongdee told Reuters.

"The attacker shot and killed both of them on the staircase."

Police were deployed to the scene while the shooting was ongoing. They found the attacker, who by then had shot himself, around 10:40, Dejrapee said.

Five people were immediately killed and at least 23 were wounded. Later, Thailand's public broadcaster and the Bangkok Post reported that an eighth victim had died.

Students shelter in classroom as gunshots heard

National police chief Gen Kittiratt Phanphet told reporters that forensic officers had found the attacker's shots were quite accurate, with several hitting vital spots on the body.

The prime minister said the attack was "well prepared" with "clear steps and clear goals".

According to local media, police have searched devices belonging to the teenager and found several videos relating to school shootings in the US.

The teenager has been described as quiet and well behaved by family members in local media.

His uncle told Thai media the teen spent much of his time indoors playing violent video games and rarely went outside. He added there was no indication the teenager was planning the attack.

The attacker had lived with his grandparents, as his parents were divorced.

The Debsirin School, founded in Bangkok in 1885, is one of Thailand's top secondary schools with branches across the country. It counts many prominent Thai figures among its alumni, from diplomats and athletes to several prime ministers.

articles.title: What is birthright citizenship and how common is birth tourism in the US?
articles.excerpt:
US President Donald Trump has announced new executive orders aimed at ending so-called birth tourism in the US and limiting birthright citizenship for certain groups.

It is part of a renewed effort b...
articles.body_text:
US President Donald Trump has announced new executive orders aimed at ending so-called birth tourism in the US and limiting birthright citizenship for certain groups.

It is part of a renewed effort by his administration to restrict access to US citizenship after the Supreme Court shot down Trump's first attempt in June.

Birthright citizenship refers to the practice of granting citizenship to those born on US soil, with some exceptions, while birth tourism is when foreign nationals come to the US specifically to give birth and get their child citizenship.

Trump signed two executive orders, a written order issued by a president to the federal government which does not require congressional approval, on Thursday.

One expands the existing definitions of non-citizens whose children are not eligible for birthright citizenship.

It prevents the automatic citizenship of babies born in the US to two non-citizen parents if one of the parents is a member of a foreign terrorist group, is a foreign government employee, has attempted to gain citizenship through fraudulent means, or is living in US territories where citizenship is not granted by US federal law.

A few of those categories were already excluded under current birthright citizenship rules, but the one relating to membership of a foreign terrorist group could raise issues, according to Colleen Putzel-Kavanaugh, an associate policy analyst at the Migration Policy Institute, an independent nonpartisan research group.

She said it is difficult to know how, when, and by whom membership would be determined, and it is also not clear "if the onus for proof falls on the government (to prove they are a member) or the individual (to prove they are not)".

The second order, meanwhile, seeks to end the practice of birth tourism by directing the departments of state and homeland security to enhance regulations and expand enforcement against the practice.

It is already illegal to travel to the US for the purpose of giving birth.

According to the executive order, operators in the birth tourism industry use deceptive advertising to entice foreign nationals to give birth in the US.

"They promise citizenship; access to public benefits; and short-term stays in specialised facilities, hotels, or rentals, but often fail to deliver on these promises," the order says.

The principle of birthright citizenship, known in legal terms as "jus soli" or "right of the soil", is enshrined in the 14th Amendment of the US Constitution.

The law was originally meant to grant citizenship to American-born, formerly enslaved people following the American Civil War.

Currently, nearly everyone born in the US, regardless of their parents' citizenship status, is granted US citizenship - with a few exceptions.

These include children born in the US to foreign diplomats, those born to enemy soldiers during a hostile occupation of US territory, and those born in unincorporated US territories where a federal statute has not granted the right to citizenship.

People born in the US territories of Puerto Rico, Guam, and the US Virgin Islands, for example, get automatic citizenship, while those born in unincorporated American Samoa are not and are instead considered "non-citizen nationals".

Trump said on Thursday that "hundreds of thousands" of babies have been born through birth tourism in the US, without providing evidence or clarifying if that figure is annual or not.

There are no government figures specifically on women coming to the US on tourism visas to give birth, but there is data on foreign residents giving birth in the country.

These show that just over 9,500 babies were born to foreign women in the US in 2024, according to the most recent estimate, external from the Centers for Disease Control (CDC). This is based on births registered to mothers with foreign addresses.

In comparison, there were 3.7 million US births in total that same year, CDC figures show,, external meaning babies born to foreign US residents amounted to roughly 0.25% of these.

However, the MPI says the government figures are likely an undercount and that foreigners could use a US address that is not their permanent home to register a birth.

The MPI estimates, external that between 20,000 to 26,000 babies were born in the US annually as a result of birth tourism, which is about 0.5 to 0.7% of total annual births.

This figure is based on a wider review of US census data, although their study notes that it is hard to know exact numbers for certain.

"Birth tourism inherently relies on the intent of an individual to come to the US to give birth and capturing that intent in data is difficult," said Putzel-Kavanaugh.

"For some women, they may be travelling and a medical emergency could necessitate birth in the US even if their intent was to give birth back in their home country."

The Trump administration's argument against birthright citizenship when the case was before the Supreme Court in April relied heavily on the need to end birth tourism.

Solicitor General D John Sauer argued that granting everyone born on US soil citizenship has allowed the birth tourism industry to thrive and created a "whole generation of American citizens abroad with no meaningful ties to the United States".

At one point, Chief Justice John Roberts asked Sauer whether he agreed that birth tourism "has no impact on the legal analysis before us".

Sauer responded that the existence of birth tourism proves that the 14th amendment has unintended consequences that would never have been approved by its creators.

We live in a world now, Sauer said, "where eight billion people are one plane ride away from having a child who's a US citizen".

Roberts, and ultimately the high court's majority, rejected that interpretation, saying: "Well, it's a new world. It's the same Constitution."

Trump has repeatedly said the US is one of the only major countries that grants birthright citizenship.

In fact, more than 30 countries practise automatic "jus soli" and without restriction in almost all cases. They include Brazil, Argentina and Mexico, as well as most other countries in Central and South America.

The US and Canada are the only two countries considered "developed" nations by the International Monetary Fund that grant mostly unrestricted birthright citizenship.

Other countries, like the UK and Australia, allow for a modified version where citizenship is automatically granted if one parent is a citizen or permanent resident.

articles.title: Sophia Laforteza steps away from Katseye, the second member to depart this year
articles.excerpt:
Katseye vocalist Sophia Laforteza has announced she will temporarily step away from the popular girl group over mental health concerns.

The departure comes less than six months after fellow bandmate ...
articles.body_text:
Katseye vocalist Sophia Laforteza has announced she will temporarily step away from the popular girl group over mental health concerns.

The departure comes less than six months after fellow bandmate Manon Bannerman said she would go on hiatus from the ensemble, known for its global hits Gnarly, Pinky Up and Gabriela.

Laforteza "will be temporarily unable to participate in upcoming promotional activities", HYBE x Geffen Records said in a statement.

"We understand how much EYEKONS were looking forward to seeing Sophia on stage, but it is imperative that her mental health and wellness are prioritized," the label said of the Filipino-American superstar.

Yoonchae, Megan, Lara Raj, Manon, Sophia, and Daniela of Katseye attend the 2026 Grammy Awards in Los Angeles.

The label said Laforteza has been receiving "the utmost support" and consulting medical professionals, and has been advised to dedicate time to "extended rest and ongoing care to ensure a full recovery".

"While Sophia herself is eager to perform alongside her members, the health, safety, and long-term well-being of our artists will always remain our highest priority," the statement said, noting that her condition will be reassessed in September.

In a separate statement, Laforteza wrote on Instagram: "Making this decision wasn't easy, but I'm learning that health has to come first. I'm realizing that if I don't take care of my mind and body now, I won't be able to keep doing what I love the most for so long."

She added: "It means more to me than I could ever say. I promise I'm going to work as hard as I can to get through this, heal properly, and come back stronger."

The girl group formed with six members in 2023 and was nominated for two Grammy Awards last year. It now will continue events with four members.

The group has previously said its members have received multiple online death threats since they made their debut.

In February, the label announced that Katseye member Bannerman would take a temporary break to focus on her health and wellbeing, as well. She has not returned but their label has said the door will always be open.

The 23-year-old Swiss singer told fans she was "healthy" and "taking care of myself".

The group said the decision had been made following "open and thoughtful conversations together".

Supermodel Carol Alt reflects on her success with the magazine and her friendship with late editor Jule Campbell, subject of the new documentary, "Beyond the Gaze: Jule Campbell's Swimsuit Issue."

Christie Brinkley has fans mistaking her for one of her daughters in her recent Instagram post.

The 72-year-old model took to social media to share a carousel of photos of herself posing next to a vintage truck to promote her new zero-sugar prosecco line.

In the photos, Brinkley is wearing a navy blue long-sleeved top with an asymmetrical neckline, paired with matching high-waisted shorts with large gold buttons, showcasing her toned legs.

One of the photos gives a zoomed-in look at the "Parks and Recreation" actress smiling at the camera, while another gives fans a head-to-toe look at the star as she leans on the truck with her eyes closed.

Brinkley posted a carousel of pictures on Instagram to promote her new sugar-free prosecco. (Christie Brinkley Instagram)

LORI LOUGHLIN AND DAUGHTER OLIVIA JADE STUN ON RED CARPET AS FANS CAN'T GET OVER THEIR RESEMBLANCE

A third photo shows her giving the camera a sultry look as she poses with her hand in her pocket.

"I thought you were your daughter for a second!" one fan wrote in the comments section, while another added, "Please dear lord let me age like @christiebrinkley."

Brinkley gave fans a look at her whole outfit with a full-body shot of her with her eyes closed. (Christie Brinkley Instagram)

"Some things get better with age… a fine bottle of wine, a classic F100, and a gorgeous Christie . 🍷❤️🔥" a third fan wrote.

Earlier this year, Brinkley shared a mirror selfie of her in a black bikini top and matching shorts, to show off the "special mirror that took over 20 years to make" from items she found on the beach while in Turks and Caicos.

Brinkley flashed the camera a sultry look in one of the photos. (Christie Brinkley Instagram)

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Fans were once again amazed by Brinkley's ageless beauty, with one fan calling her a "goddess" in the comments section.

The iconic supermodel recently spoke with Social Life magazine about her new philosophy on relationships after going through four divorces.

One of Brinkley's followers said they mistook her for her daughter in the comments section. (Kristina Bumphrey/Variety via Getty Images)

She explained that while she is still "a believer in soulmates," she isn't sure "if they last forever in the way that I thought they would."

"I also believe that soulmates can transform and still be soulmates even though it’s not the romantic soulmate anymore," she said.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Brinkley shared her philosophy on soulmates has changed after four divorces. (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for UMG)

Brinkley has been married four times: to Jean-François Allaux, Billy Joel, Richard Taubman and Peter Cook.

She has three kids; Alexa Ray, Sailor and Jack.

Lori A. Bashian is an entertainment news writer at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: WNBPA issues statement embracing diversity and inclusion amid trans athlete debate in women's sports
articles.excerpt: Transgender activists confront and harass women's sports advocates during a rally in Minneapolis. XX-XY Athletics founder Jennifer Sey and ambassador Kendall Kotzmacher detail how counter-protesters s...
articles.body_text:
Transgender activists confront and harass women's sports advocates during a rally in Minneapolis. XX-XY Athletics founder Jennifer Sey and ambassador Kendall Kotzmacher detail how counter-protesters screamed in their faces, tore their signs, and followed them to their cars outside the Target Center. The group was there to support WNBA star Sophie Cunningham for advocating for sex-protected spaces in female sports.

The Women's National Basketball Players Association issued a statement on Friday praising the "different lived experiences, cultures, lifestyles, and opinions" in the wake of the trans-athlete debate reaching the league.

"To everyone who loves this game: The WNBPA represents 200+ individual people with different lived experiences, cultures, lifestyles, and opinions. We embrace justice , equity, diversity, and inclusion. Those are the values that unite this Union and allow it to protect women's sports while creating transformational change," the WNBPA said in its statement.

"Hate, abuse, and demonization of any person or group of people, including transgender people, only fuel fear, division, and harm. We will continue to have hard conversations. But we will not be used as political pawns.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Sophie Cunningham signs autographs for fans ahead of the Indiana Fever's game against the Portland Fever on Friday. (Jaime Valdez-Imagn Images)

Support the Players. Support the Fans. At games, notify security if you witness hateful, violent, or abusive behavior. Online, report abusive posts and drown out the bots and bad actors. At home, tell your elected officials to strengthen Title IX."

The statement comes more than two weeks after a quote from Sophie Cunningham was released in an article in which she said "young girls...shouldn't have to go against biological men" in sports.

"I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men," Cunningham said.

Sophie Cunningham #8 of the Indiana Fever looks on against the Minnesota Lynx in the fourth quarter at Target Center on August 02, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Lynx defeated the Fever 108-100. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) (David Berding/Getty Images)

WOMEN'S ADVOCACY LEADER ASKS 'WHY HAVE A WNBA IF WE'RE GOING TO ALLOW GUYS IN' AMID TRANS DEBATE

"I'll always believe in that. It's really important to protect children, and that's little girls who are also involved in that category."

The WNBPA's statement also came shortly after former NBA big man Enes Kanter Freedom announced on social media that he was declaring for the WNBA draft, saying he has met all the eligibility requirements and just needs to simply identify as a woman.

Ever since Cunningham's comments, numerous players and coaches have been outspoken before, during, and after games, with many apparently disagreeing with Cunningham.

Rallies supporting Cunningham have been held prior to several of her games ever since the comments were unearthed.

Megan Rapinoe recently criticized Cunningham for taking a photo with Riley Gaines, who competed against trans swimmer Lia Thomas in college.

Former US women's national team player Megan Rapinoe gave her take on the US men's team's World Cup loss to Belgium. (Photo by Soobum Im/USSF/Getty Images))

"I don't know Sophie, so I can only project what I see about her beliefs based on her actions, and seeing a picture of her with Riley Gaines after the game told me everything I need to know about what's happening," Rapinoe said.

articles.title: US police officer accused of killing three people in Mexico arrested at border
articles.excerpt:
Chad Eberle of Texas charged over deadly shooting in Saltillo that officials say stemmed from custody dispute

A Texas police officer has been arrested in Mexico after authorities there accused him of...
articles.body_text:
Chad Eberle of Texas charged over deadly shooting in Saltillo that officials say stemmed from custody dispute

A Texas police officer has been arrested in Mexico after authorities there accused him of killing three people and critically injuring the mother of his child in what investigators say stemmed from a dispute over the custody of the minor.

The Coahuila attorney general’s office said 35-year-old Chad Eberle was arrested on Wednesday at the border on a warrant accusing him of femicide and qualified homicide, according to La Razon de Mexico, a newspaper based in Mexico City. Under Mexican law, femicide refers to the intentional killing of a woman or girl because of her gender.

According to La Razon, the deadly shooting happened in July in Saltillo, Mexico, after an argument over Eberle allegedly not having permission to take his three-year-old son. Two women and one man were killed in the attack.

The victims were identified by La Razon with the first names and ages of Ana Laura, 44; Laura Jaquelín, 22; and Emanuel, 44. The child’s 26-year-old mother was also shot in the head and remained in critical condition, officials said.

Investigators said Eberle was arrested while attempting to cross from Mexico into Texas through the international bridge at Piedras Negras, across from Eagle Pass, KTXS reported. Eberle had left the residence with his son in a gray Chevrolet Silverado, prompting investigators to launch a manhunt as they tracked the vehicle toward the Texas border, the US Sun reported.

He was then intercepted before he could re-enter the US with the child. The three-year-old was unharmed and was later placed in the care of Coahuila’s child welfare agency.

The San Antonio Express identified Eberle as a police officer in the central Texas town of Santa Anna. Before that, he worked as a deputy constable with Bexar county – which includes San Antonio – and also served as a police officer for the Northside independent school district.

The Express reported that Eberle also held law enforcement positions in the Texas communities of Somerset, Marble Falls, Gregory, near Corpus Christi, Lockney in the state’s panhandle, and Bangs in the west. According to the newspaper, a 2022 Facebook post from the Lockney police department described Eberle as an army veteran.

In a social media post on Thursday, Coahuila attorney general Federico Fernández said: “It is reported that at [9.59p] Chad ‘N’ has been admitted to the Saltillo men’s penitentiary in compliance with [an] arrest warrant, where he has been placed at the disposal of the competent judicial authority, in accordance with the corresponding procedure.”

He added: “Likewise, the minor is already in the city of Saltillo, under the custody and care of the prosecutor’s office for boys, girls and the family (Pronnif), in order to guarantee the comprehensive protection of his rights.”

Texas news outlet Coleman Today obtained a statement from Santa Anna city officials which described Eberle as “one of our reserve officers … [who] was on a personal leave of absence until December.

“The Santa Anna police department has been in contact with the US consulate in Mexico and [the Texas commission on law enforcement].”

That statement also said Eberle was “an unpaid reserve police officer hired in November 2025 and worked one weekend per month.

“Due to the ongoing investigation, no other public comment will be made.”

articles.title: Missing Illinois kayakers found dead near strait called Death's Door known for shipwrecks
articles.excerpt: A tragic boat capsizing near Alcatraz Island in San Francisco Bay has left one person dead and three missing, prompting a massive multi-agency search. Senior correspondent Claudia Cowan reports live, ...
articles.body_text:
A tragic boat capsizing near Alcatraz Island in San Francisco Bay has left one person dead and three missing, prompting a massive multi-agency search. Senior correspondent Claudia Cowan reports live, detailing how the 49-foot cabin cruiser was carrying 20 adults for a memorial service when it overturned due to rough seas. Authorities are investigating the exact cause, with recovery efforts ongoing in the frigid waters.

The bodies of an Illinois couple, both 20, who had gone missing on a kayaking trip in Lake Michigan near a strait called Death’s Door in Wisconsin were recovered earlier this week.

David Thalman, 20, and Francesca Warick, 20, were found on Monday morning off Washington Island after they went missing over the weekend, according to a joint press release from the Door County Sheriff’s Office and Washington Island Police Department.

Washington Island is located across from the Door Peninsula. Kayakers leaving from the Door Peninsula must cross the Death’s Door strait, which is known for being turbulent, to reach Washington Island.

Authorities don't believe either one was wearing life jackets.

10-YEAR-OLD BOY'S BODY PULLED FROM NEW JERSEY RIVER AS RESCUERS SEARCH FOR HIS SISTER

David Thalman and Francesca Warick's bodies were found after they went missing on a kayaking trip. (David Thalman/Facebook)

Hundreds of shipwrecks are believed to have happened in the notorious strait since the 19th century.

The Door County Sheriff’s Office said it had assumed command of the search after it turned into a recovery operation on Sunday.

Jane Lee, broker-owner of a RE/MAX office in Chicago suburb Lake Bluff, told FOX 32 that Thalman was a great employee.

"You don't see a lot of young people like that anymore today," she said. "He's very focused, always on time. We trust him 100 percent."

She said is family has a cabin on Washington Island and she started to get worried when he hadn’t answered her calls and texts about work after he left for the weekend.

Authorites don't believe Thalman and Warick were wearing life jackets when they went missing. (Madelaine Marie/Facebook)

FLORIDA KAYAKER'S GRISLY FIND IDENTIFIED AS WOMAN MISSING FOR DECADES - NOW COPS HUNT HER KILLER

"That moment I did worry," she said, adding that when her office heard the news, "We all cried. Everybody was in shock."

Warick, a twin, "brought joy to everyone around her," according to her obituary.

A view from Washington Island, Wisconsin. (Education Images/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

"She was a bright, happy, and free-spirited young woman whose beautiful smile and kind heart left a lasting impression on all who knew her. She loved her family deeply and treasured every moment spent with them."

Authorities said the couple likely drowned. Their deaths remain under investigation.

Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Ebola cases top 4,000 in DRC as WHO urges Ervebo vaccine trial
articles.excerpt:
The number of confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 4,000, according to government data, as the world’s second-largest outbreak shows no sign of slowing.

A...
articles.body_text:
The number of confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 4,000, according to government data, as the world’s second-largest outbreak shows no sign of slowing.

As health authorities remain on alert, World Health Organization (WHO) vaccine experts on Friday recommended a full-scale human trial of the only existing approved Ebola vaccine to see if it could offer cross-protection against the deadly Bundibugyo strain spreading in DRC, a strain for which there is no vaccine.

DRC reported 4,053 Bundibugyo cases, including 1,850 deaths, since the outbreak was declared in mid-May, the latest Ministry of Health situation report showed.

The outbreak has hit 53 health zones across five provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. Eighty-seven percent of cases are in Ituri province, the epicentre of the current outbreak, with 11 percent in neighbouring North Kivu.

The epidemic has been described as the ⁠fastest-spreading on record, and experts believe the true number of cases may be much ‌higher than the official tally.

So far only West Africa’s 2014-2016 outbreak has been bigger, with more than 28,000 cases recorded ‌across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

The disease response has also faced challenges including the country’s military conflict, delayed detection and a lack of readily available treatments and vaccines, as Ebola spreads through contact with bodily fluids.

On Friday, the WHO recommended the commencement of full-scale human trials for the Ervebo vaccine, the only licensed Ebola vaccine.

Ervebo has proven to be safe and efficacious against the more common Zaire strain of the Ebola virus, and WHO experts said early data, notably from animal trials, showed it may also give some protection against the rare Bundibugyo strain.

Across several studies, the experts found that three out of four non-human primates vaccinated with Ervebo survived the Bundibugyo strain, compared with one out of four control animals. An unpublished study on ferrets the experts looked at also found that the research-grade version of Ervebo provided 100 percent protection against Bundibugyo, whereas all control animals died within 10 days.

“The members recommended Ervebo, the only licensed Ebola vaccine, be prioritised for inclusion in a randomised clinical trial in the context of the ongoing outbreak,” a WHO statement said.

Still, a specific Bundibugyo vaccine is the preferred option for fighting the current outbreak, according to TAG-CVP, the United Nations’ health agency’s Technical Advisory Group on Candidate Vaccine Prioritization. As such, the group cautions against any immediate action or trials without the necessary findings to move forward.

“Expectations need to be managed about its likely protective effect if used in a Phase III ring vaccination trial, as efficacy against symptomatic disease and transmission may not be high, whereas protection against a fatal outcome may be achieved,” their report said.

Two potential Bundibugyo vaccines are in the early stages of clinical trials on humans, while a third is being worked on to bring it to that stage.

The Gavi global vaccine alliance maintains a stockpile of 500,000 Ervebo doses. It said doses from the stockpile were to be made available for the trials, with some already in the DRC.

“This is already the largest Ebola outbreak in DRC’s history, and could well become the largest outbreak ever,” said Gavi chief executive Sania Nishtar. “Given the terrible toll on communities and frontline workers, we are encouraged that the approved Ebola vaccine Ervebo … could help reduce severe illness and deaths.”

articles.title: Kidnapped rare Serbian eagle freed into wild after rescue
articles.excerpt:
Serbian peacekeepers brought him home on a military transport plane

A rare eastern imperial eagle has been rescued from animal traffickers and released back into the wild in Serbia after months in ca...
articles.body_text:
Serbian peacekeepers brought him home on a military transport plane

A rare eastern imperial eagle has been rescued from animal traffickers and released back into the wild in Serbia after months in captivity.

After leaving the nest last year, Feliks was caught in Syria by poachers who eventually demanded a ransom - which was refused.

After protracted talks the bird was taken to a wildlife centre in Beirut, Lebanon, where he recuperated for more than half a year before his repatriation on a Serbian military plane.

The protected species is critically endangered, but conservation work since 2017 has brought the population in Serbia from one pair up to 29 pairs this year, according to the Bird Protection and Study Society of Serbia (BPSSS).

In July 2025, just as the young raptor first flew the nest, experts tracked him for conservation purposes as he flew towards the Middle East.

"At that point, we started to worry because we could see that he was heading towards an extremely unsafe region," Uros Stojiljkovic of the BPSSS told the AFP news agency.

When the bird's tracking signal was lost in October, initially it was thought the tracker was faulty.

But it soon became clear Feliks had been abducted and eventually was put up for sale by poachers.

Feliks spent months in recovery before he was finally released again

Weeks passed before a partner organisation in Lebanon contacted the Serbian conservationist and said Feliks' unnamed captors had demanded a ransom.

"We categorically refused. By doing so, you are effectively supporting that smuggling chain," Stojiljkovic told AFP.

An adult eastern imperial eagle has a wingspan of six feet (2 meters)

Lengthy negotiations secured the bird's release, but not before refugees carried Feliks in a potato sack over the Nahr al-Kabir river on the northern border between Syria and Lebanon, the Associated Press reported.

In June this year, Serbian peacekeepers returning from Lebanon escorted the bird to Palic Zoo.

Feliks arrived at the zoo's shelter "exhausted, after a long and demanding transport by military plane", zoo director Sonja Mandić said in a statement, and his health was monitored daily.

After more than a month of careful recovery, Feliks was released into the wild on Thursday.

"We wish Feliks to get stronger as soon as possible, survive all the adversities, conquer his territory and leave descendants," said Milan Ružić, executive director of the BPSSS.

The young eagle will be closely monitored in the coming weeks, experts said.

Country has been divided since 2014, with rival governments in the east and west.

For more than a decade, Libya has been struggling with both conflict and deep political divisions.

A number of international diplomatic initiatives have failed to end the impasse.

It has two rival administrations, two prime ministers and two seats of government.

Now, a US plan to unify the warring parties under a power-sharing deal seems to be gathering momentum.

Alongside Washington, Turkiye has also been involved in bringing the parties together.

But is there common ground to reach a deal? Or could all this be a recipe for renewed fighting?
