articles.title: DAVID MARCUS: Why rising prices may not cost Republicans as much as you think
articles.excerpt:
Gen Z commentator CJ Pearson joins 'Saturday in America' to discuss concerns about the rise of 'affordability socialism' among young people.

The great burrito debate burst onto the social media scene...
articles.body_text:
Gen Z commentator CJ Pearson joins 'Saturday in America' to discuss concerns about the rise of 'affordability socialism' among young people.

The great burrito debate burst onto the social media scene this week after Turning Point USA's Andrew Kolvet posted that the Gen Z voters at his events are upset that the Mexican wraps cost $20 these days.

Reaction was swift, heated and mixed, with some commenters saying this proved prices and affordability are a major red flag for the GOP in the midterms. But others scolded the youths, claiming that "in their day," they survived five years on nothing but ramen noodles, peanut butter and the kindness of strangers.

The fairly obvious subtext to this debate is the war in Iran, as team "cheap burritos" insists the war must end now to bring down prices and win in November, and team "suck it up, kids" argues that long-term economic success requires winning the war.

REPUBLICANS FACE TICKING MIDTERM CLOCK AS IRAN FALLOUT KEEPS PRESSURE ON GAS PRICES

The real question, for Republicans and the Trump administration, is just how angry are Americans over prices, and will that anger make them choose Democrats over the status quo?

Andrew Kolvet, producer of 'The Charlie Kirk Show,' speaks during the public memorial service for Charlie Kirk at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona, on Sept. 21. (Patrick t. Fallon/AFP via Getty Images)

To answer this question, it is important to understand that there are two kinds of political issues: gut and mental. Crime, for example, is a gut issue, because if you don’t feel safe on the street you feel it in your gut. Foreign policy, on the other hand, for most Americans, is a mental issue in that you think about it more than you feel it.

Affordability and prices can be a gut issue, and have been in several recent elections. If you are in line at the grocery store watching the tally rack up and hoping you have enough money for it, that is something you feel in the pit of your stomach.

In the fall of 2024, I was in Bedford, Pa., talking to some voters when a woman walked into the restaurant and, apropos of nothing, announced, "I cannot believe how much I just paid for groceries," to nods and grunts of angry assent.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS WANT MAJOR CHANGE AMID ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL DISCONTENT

This was not an uncommon occurrence two years ago. Cost of living and prices were not just the top issue for most voters I spoke with, but in many cases it all but eclipsed any others because they really were feeling it. You could see it in their eyes.

In Detroit last month, voters I spoke to were not obsessed with prices. In fact, most felt that Motown was seeing a revival, which helps to explain why, despite a very narrow statewide primary victory for Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed, he lost the city badly to the more mainstream, less economically populist Rep. Haley Stevens.

Hasan Piker, a streamer and creator, appears during day two of Web Summit Vancouver 2026 at the Vancouver Convention Centre in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada, on May 13, 2026. (Sportsfile via Getty Images)

This spring, there was a three-week-or-so period when gas prices really rocketed, and it became the complaint on everyone’s tongue. It was becoming a gut issue, but then the prices eased, and since have stayed in the "I don’t love it, but I can live with it" range.

As for the young adult Gen Z voters feeling an economic pinch, they have some real complaints, even if overpriced Door-Dash meals are not chief among them. The fact is that the cost of entry into adulthood is much higher than it was 30 years ago.

DEMOCRATS LURE ‘POLITICALLY HOMELESS’ GEN Z TOWARD SOCIALISM — A COUNTERATTACK IS TAKING SHAPE

When my then-girlfriend and I moved in together in 1995, we had to pay for rent, a landline (which cost almost nothing), and a couple of utility bills. There was no internet or cell phone bill, and our only subscription was to the journal Lingua Franca.

Republicans should be able to appeal to many of these frustrated young voters with targeted economic relief, something the Trump tax cuts achieved, for example, instead of the snake oil of socialism that the newfangled Democratic Party of Hasan Piker is hawking to them.

Everybody remembers the folly of President Joe Biden telling Americans that they didn’t know how good they had it while they were tightening their belts, and part of that was that Grandpa Joe was trying to talk intellectually about what had become a gut issue.

As far as Iran goes, the only theater of this particular war that the American people really care about is the gas station. If Trump can keep prices moderate, he can lob the occasional bomb at the mullahs until the cows come home.

100 DAY SPRINT TO THE MIDTERMS KICKS OFF AS REPUBLICANS AND DEMOCRATS CLASH FOR CONTROL ACROSS THE COUNTRY

The 2026 election is becoming a stark choice between Republicans promising slow and steady progress and Democrats who want to blow up the system and start over, without a Senate, with a packed Supreme Court and with no private health insurance.

Unless something catastrophic happens between now and November, that is a choice that benefits the GOP, and it's why prices will not be as decisive as so many believe they will be.

CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM DAVID MARCUS

David Marcus is a columnist living in West Virginia and the author of "Charade: The COVID Lies That Crushed A Nation."

articles.title: These are five of the most unstoppable players from the EA Sports college football video games
articles.excerpt:
YouTuber Bordeaux discusses EA Sports adding microtransactions to College Football 27 and the fallout among the gaming community with Fox News Digital/OutKick.

Video games just aren't what they used ...
articles.body_text:
YouTuber Bordeaux discusses EA Sports adding microtransactions to College Football 27 and the fallout among the gaming community with Fox News Digital/OutKick.

Video games just aren't what they used to be, and that includes sports video games.

Nowadays, all the creativity and ingenuity has been sucked out in favor of cheap roster updates to increase profits, but it wasn't always this way.

The college football series by EA Sports in particular used to be so universally beloved that its release day in mid-July was almost a national holiday.

With the college football offseason starting to wind down, I thought it would be fun to relive some of the best players the game ever had to offer.

And I'm not talking "oh yeah, that guy was pretty good," either.

I'm referring to the players who were banned from your head-to-head matches with your group of friends. The players who caused more broken controllers than your average "Dark Souls" boss.

Obviously, up until a few years ago, the players in the NCAA football games never had names, but you knew exactly who they were.

With all that in mind, let's dig up some childhood trauma with five completely broken college football video game characters.

Quinshon Judkins #1 of the Ohio State Buckeyes celebrates with teammates after scoring a touchdown in the first quarter against the Texas Longhorns during the Goodyear Cotton Bowl at AT&T Stadium on January 10, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Alex Slitz/Getty Images)

When "College Football 25" was nearing its release date, certain influencers were able to test the game early and came back with a few notes to share with their followers.

Nearly unanimously, every content creator seemed to agree that "Quinshon Judkins was broken."

What the rest of the general public quickly found out was, these influencers weren't just mining for clicks.

Quinshon Judkins really was broken, particularly his spin move.

ONE OF THESE EIGHT COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS WILL BE HOISTING THE NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP TROPHY IN 2026

Video after video was posted on social media showing off Judkins turning into a Beyblade the minute the spin button was pressed, as All-American defenders bounced off the Ohio State running back as if he was a waterbed rolling downhill.

The move was so broken that players across the country started online petitions to try and get the EA developers to nerf Judkins' spinning.

I'm not playing this up, either. If you Google "Quinshon Judkins" one of the first suggested searches that pops up is "spin move 'College Football 25.'"

You know you've made it as a video game character when you make the general public rage-quit so badly they have to resort to petitions to try and stop you.

Jan 4, 2006; Pasadena, CA, USA; Texas Longhorns quarterback (10) Vince Young runs past Southern California Trojans linebackers (45) Oscar Lua and (55) Keith Rivers during the 4th quarter of the Rose Bowl Game at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, California. (Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports)

Before Tim Tebow, before Cam Newton, and absolutely before Johnny Football, there was Vince Young (or should I say, QB#10).

The Texas Longhorns' signal caller was a 6'5", 235 lb cyborg who ran a 4.5-second 40-yard dash and threw a football harder than most high school pitchers threw a fastball.

The man was unstoppable in real-life, but he might have been even more broken in "NCAA 06."

He was a 95 overall rated workhorse who was faster than anyone in your defensive front seven, and had the arm strength to fit the ball into any window you could think of.

Sports video game fans talk about how ungodly Michael Vick was in "Madden 04," but VY was essentially the college football answer to Vick in video game format.

Couple all of that with the fact that Young had the "impact player" label attached to him - back when that moniker actually meant something from a gameplay perspective - and even when you thought you had him dead to rights, the Texas gunslinger would turn into Houdini and you'd send your controller through the window.

Almost makes you feel sorry for that USC defensive staff in the Rose Bowl.

The West Virginia Mountaineers logo on a helmet during the Guaranteed Rate Bowl college football game between the West Virginia Mountaineers and the Minnesota Golden Gophers on December 28, 2021 at Chase Field in Phoenix, Arizona. (Kevin Abele/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

This one might seem like a bit of a copout, but it's absolutely the right call.

If you're familiar with any of my writing, you know all about the 2007 West Virginia football team and how close that team was to immortal glory.

The video game version of that team was just as good, too, and for all the same reasons.

The four-headed monster of quarterback Pat White, running backs Steve Slaton and Noel Devine, and fullback Owen Schmitt were so dynamic that you rarely if ever had to call a pass play to dominate a game.

White, Slaton, and Devine all had 90+ speed ratings, so running a triple option out of shotgun in a two-back set made your offense virtually untouchable.

When you brought the brickhouse that was Schmitt in for short yardage situations or subbed him in at tight end or H-back, all bases were covered and it was truly over from that point on.

WHAT DOES A REALISTICALLY SUCCESSFUL FIRST YEAR LOOK LIKE FOR HEAD COACH LANE KIFFIN AT LSU?

Each player did awesome things on their own, but when combined into a single rushing attack, the sum was always greater than its parts.

In that sense, the West Virginia backfield in "NCAA 08" was basically college football's version of The Avengers, so have fun trying to stop that.

PHILADELPHIA, PA - DECEMBER 23: Jadeveon Clowney #90 of the Houston Texans walks on the field prior to the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on December 23, 2018 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Eagles defeated the Texans 32-30. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images)

You didn't think they were going to be all offensive players, did you?

While it's true that offense always garnered the bulk of the attention in the college football video games, there were plenty of defensive players that made the game unforgettable, and none more so than South Carolina's Jadeveon Clowney.

In the dying embers of the old "NCAA" series before its revival in 2023, Clowney was a god amongst mortals, making the Gamecocks' defense elite almost by himself.

You could make the argument that the video game version of Clowney was even more elite than his real life counterpart, and that's saying quite a lot because the man was a beast in college.

Rated 99 overall, Clowney had 91 strength, 94 acceleration, and 99 finesse moves, meaning he was able to either toss your offensive tackle aside or swim move around him at lightning speeds.

And his 99 hit power rating almost guaranteed the ball was coming out when he got to your player.

When I say the man was broken, he was truly broken.

Double teams, chipping with the tight end or a running back, it didn't matter, Clowney was getting to your quarterback.

Prayer was your only chance against South Carolina's defense in "NCAA 14."

Reggie Bush (5) of the University of Southern California celebrates his touchdown against the University of Texas during the BCS National Championship Game at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, CA. Texas defeated USC 41-38 for the national title. (Jamie Schwaberow/NCAA Photos via Getty Images)

For some of my older readers who played the original "Tecmo Bowl" back in the 1980s, Reggie Bush in "NCAA 06" was basically Bo Jackson on steroids and crack.

Mind you, this was before "locamotion" and all the fancy physics engines, so a player with 99 speed and insane moves like Bush could literally stop on a dime, spin move a defender five yards into the sideline, then speed away from his pursuers.

I almost made a rule that only one player from a given year could make this list, but I couldn't leave both Vince Young and Reggie Bush out.

The 2005 Heisman Trophy winner was a literal cheat code in "NCAA 06," so much so that I remember multiple friends from my school outright banning the use of USC during head-to-head matches.

I would be remiss if I didn't mention Bush's impact player label, too, meaning he went from a mere superhuman to a mythical creature with the ball in his hands.

Reggie Bush was, hands down, the most broken player in any NCAA Football game and you would be hard-pressed to tell me otherwise.

articles.title: Mark Halperin calls Hasan Piker a 'horrible person' as Democrats face pressure to distance from streamer
articles.excerpt:
Journalist and "2WAY" host Mark Halperin called Hasan Piker a "horrible" person on Thursday and suggested he might be an exception to his "presumption of grace to all" rule.

Journalist and "2WAY" hos...
articles.body_text:
Journalist and "2WAY" host Mark Halperin called Hasan Piker a "horrible" person on Thursday and suggested he might be an exception to his "presumption of grace to all" rule.

Journalist and "2WAY" host Mark Halperin called far-left streamer Hasan Piker a "horrible person" and said he was a possible exception to his rule about showing a presumption of grace to all.

"That's kind of our mantra here, show the presumption of grace to all, with the possible exception of Hasan Piker, the more I learn about the guy, the more I believe he is an exception to the rule that we should be showing the presumption of grace to all. He seems to be a horrible person," Halperin said during a "2Way Tonight" conversation.

Halperin called him "over the top" and noted the streamer's ties to Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, who he has campaigned with.

2026 MIDTERMS STATE OF PLAY: KEY RACES UNFOLD AS STEVENS, EL-SAYED BATTLE IN MICHIGAN

El-Sayed is also endorsed by several prominent Democrats, including Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Sen. Bernie Sanders.

Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., (L) and influencer and left-wing political commentator Hasan Piker (C) stand with Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong during a campaign rally for Hong on Aug. 2, 2026. (Joshua Lott/Getty Images)

Hyma Moore told Halperin during the conversation that Democrats were going to need to make a difficult decision about Piker.

"So I think what politicians are going to have to say now is, look, is it more important for us to connect with Hasan Piker's large audience or should we just stop giving him a platform to build on?" he said. "I think Democrats are going to have to make a hard decision. What's more important? Expanding the audience or having Hasan have this large platform where he is starting to be really irresponsible with."

Kavian Shroff, a moderate Democratic political analyst who worked on Hillary Clinton's campaign, told Fox News Digital in a statement that Piker is a huge electoral liability for the Democratic Party.

JAMES CARVILLE VOWS TO ABANDON DEMOCRATIC PARTY IF FAR-LEFT HASAN PIKER BECOMES LEADING VOICE

"Piker is a huge electoral liability for Democrats. He may help candidates on the farther left get attention and online support during the primaries, but as we are already seeing in Michigan, Republicans would much rather run against a figure like Piker than the actual candidate on the ballot. That’s why it’s a problem when folks like Abdul El-Sayed campaign so closely with him, because then it’s hard to draw real distance from that line of attack," Schroff said.

Schroff said Piker hated the party and argued he spent more time attacking moderate Democrats than Republicans.

Twitch streamer Hasan Piker is facing renewed scrutiny after viewers spotted a framed newspaper front page from Sept. 12, 2001, in his background. (Sam Barnes/Web Summit via Sportsfile via Getty Images)

"I was a 2024 DNC delegate and I think a lot of Democrats are still traumatized by that loss and blame it on losing ground online and with young men particularly. That has created a lot of insecurity where Democrats are embracing figures like Piker out of a sort of desperation, but it won’t serve us in the long run," he added.

Schroff pointed to Piker's "vile comments" about 9/11 and said Piker "joked about sex with minors, and repeatedly spread disinformation." He also pointed to Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-VT., admitting during a CNN interview that Piker had a large following that could reach voters.

HASAN PIKER, ABDUL EL-SAYED MOCK JAMES CARVILLE THREATENING TO LEAVE DEMOCRATS AND 'SWEETENING THE DEAL'

"He has no place in our party, and I’d encourage other Democrats to think about what their values are here," he said. "When it comes down to it, it’s pretty sad to see folks like Bernie Sanders defend Piker, acknowledging he has toxic views but reverting to ‘he has a whole lot of followers’ as a justification for aligning and campaigning with him."

Sanders was asked during a CNN interview on Tuesday if he was comfortable with Piker's 9/11 remarks. The streamer once said America deserved 9/11.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"I think that's a dumb statement," Sanders said. "On the other hand, he has a whole lot of followers and a lot of things that he's saying that are making sense to a lot of people. I think, you know, we have to get above cancel culture. You know, when you're doing radio, whatever they do, podcasts three hours a day, you say dumb things."

"I suspect if you go back over your career, there may be one or two things that you've said that you may have regretted," the senator told CNN's Abby Phillip. "But I think what we have got to do is look at the totality of where people are coming from and go forward."

Hanna Panreck is an associate editor at Fox News.

articles.title: Italy vows to maintain border checks despite Spain’s countermeasures threat
articles.excerpt:
How the far right weaponised the Ceuta crisis

Italy has doubled down on its temporary reinstatement of border controls following the deadly rush of thousands of migrants into the Spanish enclave of C...
articles.body_text:
How the far right weaponised the Ceuta crisis

Italy has doubled down on its temporary reinstatement of border controls following the deadly rush of thousands of migrants into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, even after Madrid threatened retaliation.

In a statement on Friday, the Italian government said it would not bow to “ultimatums or impositions” from ⁠Spain and would maintain border controls until at least August 15.

The refusal came hours after the Spanish government declared a two-day deadline for Italy “to rectify, put an end to the checks and treat Spaniards like other European citizens”.

“If it does not do so before the end of Sunday, August 9, Spain will be obliged to adopt proportional measures to protect the interests and dignity of its citizens,” Spain’s statement said.

The diplomatic tit-for-tat unfolds as Spain continues to reel from the influx of some 72,000 people who crossed into Ceuta from Morocco last week, on foot and by sea.

Mass arrivals in the North African Spanish enclave angered other European Union leaders who have taken a hard anti-migration stance, including far-right Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.

Italy earlier said it would temporarily reintroduce border checks with Spain starting on August 1 in what Meloni called an “extraordinary measure” seeking to “safeguard national security and prevent possible repercussions for our nation”.

Yet experts said there was little prospect of migrants travelling from Ceuta to Italy, particularly as Italy and Spain do not share a land border. Rights groups instead pegged Meloni’s move as “political theatre”.

Still, 22 EU member states signed a joint letter accusing Spain of “pull factors” that destabilise the bloc’s borders.

The vast majority of the Ceuta migrants have since returned to Morocco as authorities tallied at least 100 deaths.

Also on Friday, Spain said its police successfully dismantled a people-smuggling operation believed to have brought 2,000 migrants into the country via Spain’s southeastern coast and the island of Ibiza.

Amid the political fallout, Spanish leaders are grappling with a humanitarian crisis still ongoing in Ceuta.

Of the few thousand undocumented migrants who remain in the enclave, at least 1,342 are children, Youth Minister Sira Rego said on Friday – hundreds of whom are unaccompanied.

Rego acknowledged “painful images” of children sleeping on Ceuta’s streets, noting that two schools had been opened as authorities evaluated more locations as possible reception centres.

Still, Ceuta authorities said at least 1,100 children needed assistance, with Ceuta’s theoretical capacity only totalling 90 places where people could be housed.

“It might only be a matter of a few weeks before we start seeing [children] transferred to and welcomed on the mainland,” Rego told reporters.

Local and international charities have cautioned that the children face abuse and exploitation.

Jose Miguel Morales, head of Federacion Sur Acoge, a migrant rights and assistance group in southern Spain, said some of the children were under 14 years old and had already been beaten and assaulted.

But the transfer of children to the mainland has become a domestic flashpoint in Madrid, where Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s government approved 25 million euros ($29m) to help support unaccompanied minors in the territory.

Leaders from the far-right, anti-immigration Vox party were quick to say they opposed any aid for migrant children.

Vox leader Santiago Abascal wrote on X that “not one euro from Spaniards” should go “for illegals, for invaders”.

articles.title: Private man with a public life Dak Prescott addresses broken engagement publicly for the first time
articles.excerpt:
Dak Prescott found George Pickens for a 38-yard TD to give the Dallas Cowboys the lead over the Los Angeles Chargers.

Dak Prescott is a private individual by nature but he's blessed with the ability ...
articles.body_text:
Dak Prescott found George Pickens for a 38-yard TD to give the Dallas Cowboys the lead over the Los Angeles Chargers.

Dak Prescott is a private individual by nature but he's blessed with the ability to play quarterback for the Dallas Cowboys, making him a public figure. And those two truths collided earlier this year when his canceled marriage engagement became gossip column fodder.

Prescott addressed the issue for the first time on Thursday and, in typical fashion, declined to reveal everything that happened, including why the engagement to Sarah Jane Ramos was called off and by whom.

But he did show regret that the private situation became so public and added we shouldn't believe everything we read afterward.

Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) celebrates a touchdown during the first half of an NFL football game against the Washington Redskins in Arlington, Texas, Sunday, Dec. 15, 2019. (AP Photo/Ron Jenkins)

NOTHING TO SEE HERE: COWBOYS QUARTERBACK DAK PRESCOTT AND HIS EX'S BRIDESMAID ARE JUST FRIENDS

"Yeah, I mean, I don't necessarily think it was public to me," Prescott told reporters who cover the team, via the Dallas Morning News.

"Once again, I believe what you take in, what you read, what you look up, you're doing that to yourself. There were a lot of false narratives out there on both of our sides. That was very unfortunate. Unfortunate for me, but somebody who's been [dealing with the media] and knows how to [handle] it … And unfortunate for her.

"But it's kind of the life we live in. Yeah, it was an unfortunate situation for obviously everybody. More importantly, the kids. And so for me, it's just about making sure I'm there in every which way for them."

Prescott became engaged to Ramos in October 2024 and the couple welcomed two daughters together and planned an April 2026 wedding in Lake Como, Italy.

The engagement was called off in March 2026, roughly five weeks before the ceremony. A representative for Ramos told People that the split was a mutual decision and the couple remained committed to co-parenting their children, describing both as "heartbroken" by the end of the relationship.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Sarah Jane Ramos and Dak Prescott pose for a photo before Dak Prescott's Faith Fight Finish Foundation 2024 Gala at Thompson Hotel Dallas on May 17, 2024 in Dallas, Texas. (Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images for Faith Fight Finish Foundation)

Other reports painted a different picture of what led to the breakup. TMZ reported that the relationship had been "rocky behind the scenes for months" and that it reached a breaking point after a blowup argument during the couple's joint bachelor and bachelorette trip to the Bahamas.

Who called off the engagement and why was the stuff of subsequent and perhaps unfounded speculation.

Whatever the reasons, it's obvious Prescott's focus, aside from playing for the Cowboys and winning, is his children.

Margaret Jane Rose Prescott was born in February 2024. Prescott has said her birth changed his outlook on life, centering him less on himself and more on her.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott (4) throws a pass under pressure from Green Bay Packers defensive end Micah Parsons (1) in the first half of an NFL football game Sunday, Sept. 28, 2025, in Arlington, Texas. (AP Photo/Jeffrey McWhorter)

Aurora Rayne Prescott was born in May 2025. Her middle name is Rayne because that is the quarterback's legal first name: Rayne Dakota Prescott.

Prescott and his ex-fiancee are co-parenting the girls so they remain a big part of Prescott's life, including during this Cowboys training camp which they have visited.

"I appreciate them getting a chance to, you know, come to my office or, you know, come out on the football field and just hang for a little bit, even if they don't fully grasp it," Prescott said. "They'll have these memories and stuff like that in the back of their heads.

"And, um, MJ, I mean, she's, excuse me, the oldest, she's already, yeah, she enjoys the, the football side of it, saying the number 4, showing it. And then, I think, even just seeing her dad on pictures and in places."

It is clear that Prescott wants to win for himself, and his teammates. But he wants everyone to understand he also wants to win for his children.

"That's who I want to win for," he repeated. "You know, it was for a long time, wanting to win for myself and the approval of people, or to prove myself right. I want those girls to say their dad's a champion."

FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.

articles.title: Spain threatens retaliation if Italy fails to lift border controls after Ceuta crossings
articles.excerpt:
Hundreds of migrants were pictured lined up on a beach in Ceuta to collect aid

Spain has threatened to impose counter-measures on Italy if it fails to lift border controls introduced following the ma...
articles.body_text:
Hundreds of migrants were pictured lined up on a beach in Ceuta to collect aid

Spain has threatened to impose counter-measures on Italy if it fails to lift border controls introduced following the mass crossing of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta.

Roughly 78,000 migrants from neighbouring Morocco arrived in Ceuta by sea in a matter of hours on Thursday and Friday last week.

In the wake of the crossings, which saw around 100 people die, Italy partially suspended its Schengen arrangement with Spain, which included the closure of maritime and air entry points as well as the reinforcement of land border controls.

On Friday, Spain called the move "unjustified" and "discriminatory against the Spanish population" and demanded it be reversed by Sunday 9 August.

It added it would introduce "proportionate measures to protect the interests and dignity of its citizens" if Italy failed to reverse its decision.

The statement did not specify what these reprisals would be.

Italy promptly responded to Spain's warning, saying it would not accept "ultimatums or impositions" from Madrid and that it plans to keep border checks in place until at least 15 August - when it said Spain "expected a new wave of migration" to hit Ceuta.

Watch: Migrants started to return to Morocco after thousands entered Spain's Ceuta on 30 July

Italy, which does not share a land border with Spain, said its decision to partially suspend the EU's ​border-free Schengen arrangements was to prevent any of the migrants who had entered Ceuta from travelling on to Italy.

Madrid dismissed this position, saying it was based on "spurious arguments" that lacked any basis in fact because the migrants who entered Ceuta had no way of entering the Schengen area. It added the vast majority of migrants have already returned to Morocco.

Last week's crossings marked a new low in relations between Spain's socialist leader Pedro Sanchez and Italy's conservative leader Giorgia Meloni - who has long called for stricter migration rules in the EU.

It remains unclear exactly why tens of thousands of migrants attempted to cross into Ceuta, but the EU's Migration Commissioner Magnus Brunner has suggested criminal networks spreading disinformation were to blame - an assertion the Spanish government has agreed with.

The crossings came after Spain's Supreme Court ruled that migrants stopped at sea while trying to reach Ceuta or Melilla cannot be summarily returned to Morocco.

The two exclaves have long been a bone of diplomatic contention between Spain and Morocco, which does not recognise Spanish sovereignty over them.

The number of people swimming to Ceuta at once has raised questions about why Morocco's border guards did not attempt to stop them

The Ceuta crossings have also caused a diplomatic rift among EU nations that share open borders as part of the Schengen area.

Italy's decision to suspend its agreement was backed by Finland and Denmark, while the Czech Republic called for Spain's membership to be temporarily suspended.

Morocco, for its part, has laid blame for the crisis on Spain's Supreme Court, with an unnamed government source briefing local outlets that "the deterrent element of the system collapsed and the dam gave way, not under the weight of the criminals, but of a judge's decision".

Meanwhile, Moroccan media is reporting fresh online calls to co-ordinate another mass border-crossing attempt, similar to what was seen before the influx last week.

Nearly 1,400 minors, some of them "very young boys and girls",  still remain in Ceuta following last week's crossings, Spanish Youth Minister Sira Rego said on Friday.

She added: "There was a situation in which the system was overwhelmed, but it is now being brought under control. It is true that there are many boys and girls, and the procedure takes time.

"We wanted to make clear that we have prioritized the most vulnerable cases."

articles.title: Drew Rasmussen and the Rays look to exploit Logan Gilbert's home struggles against the Mariners
articles.excerpt:
Bret Boone says he's jealous of current MLB players access to film and analytics.

We are a week into August, and we are significantly closer to the end of the baseball season than the beginning. Over...
articles.body_text:
Bret Boone says he's jealous of current MLB players access to film and analytics.

We are a week into August, and we are significantly closer to the end of the baseball season than the beginning. Overall, this has been a good year of betting, with July and August giving me back some of the units I lost to bad luck earlier in the year. That's part of the reason I enjoy betting every day — eventually it will balance out. As long as we are under control, we can be profitable. I'm looking for more profit as the Rays take on the Mariners.

The Tampa Bay Rays are one of the best teams in baseball, and they continue to show that a properly run team can do anything. Regardless of the "market," a team, when built correctly, can be productive and have sustained success. The Rays don't have a ton of big names, but they do have good pitchers and hitters that are under control and peaking at the same time. You don't always have to spend millions on guys to be great; you just have to have good scouting and some luck.

Tampa Bay Rays starter Drew Rasmussen pitches against the Baltimore Orioles during the first inning of a baseball game Sunday, Aug. 14, 2022, in St. Petersburg, Fla. (AP Photo/Steve Nesius)

One of their best pitchers is taking the ball today as Drew Rasmussen heads to the hill. For the season, Rasmussen is 10-5 with a 2.91 ERA and a 0.93 WHIP. This is a fantastic season for him, as he currently is 16th in wins, 12th in ERA, third in WHIP, and 29th in strikeouts. He has always been a solid arm for the Rays, but gets less attention than some of the other ones who have been anchors of the Tampa rotation over the years. Mariners hitters haven't been great against Rasmussen, batting just .222 over 45 at-bats. His former teammate, Randy Arozarena, has the best history against him, going 3-for-7, but all of them were singles.

The Seattle Mariners shouldn't be this bad. I really don't know what is going on with this team. They have plenty of pitching. Their lineup has more than enough talent, but for whatever reason, they aren't performing the way they need to. Cal Raleigh has had a rough year, but that's one guy. There are many more that aren't playing quite as well as expected. They traded for Taylor Ward at the deadline to give them a bit of a boost. The AL West is the easiest division to win, so they should still have a chance, despite being four games under .500 at the moment.

Seattle Mariners starting pitcher Logan Gilbert reacts after a batted ball was trapped beneath his jersey against the Athletics during the first inning at T-Mobile Park in Seattle, Wash., on April 22, 2026. The play was ruled a hit. (Joe Nicholson/Imagn Images)

I think the Mariners probably should be better because of this rotation. Their team is loaded with good arms. Logan Gilbert, tonight's starter, is just one of the talented players they have. He is 8-6 for the year with a 3.46 ERA, and a 0.99 WHIP. He also has 139 strikeouts for the season. To compare to Rasmussen, he is 23rd in ERA, 15th in strikeouts, and fifth in WHIP. He is worse at home than on the road, allowing 16 of his 17 homers in Seattle. Tampa has been very good against the Mariners righty, batting .296 against him.

Junior Caminero of the Tampa Bay Rays grounds out to the pitcher during the first inning of the MLB All-Star Game at Citizens Bank Park in Philadelphia, Pa., on July 14, 2026. (Al Bello/Getty Images)

There aren't a ton of guys that stand out against Gilbert, but like most things the Rays do, they are better as a team. I think this is a good opportunity to take Rasmussen and the Rays tonight. Gilbert has been very good, but he has allowed multiple runs in each of his past four starts. He also is more vulnerable at home this season than on the road. Give me the Rays tonight.

articles.title: Martha Stewart questions Meghan Markle’s homemaking credentials with blunt career assessment
articles.excerpt:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Martha Stewart is not entirely convinced Meghan Markle’s path into the lifestyle world adds up.

The 85-year-old homemaking icon off...
articles.body_text:
Fox News Flash top entertainment and celebrity headlines are here.

Martha Stewart is not entirely convinced Meghan Markle’s path into the lifestyle world adds up.

The 85-year-old homemaking icon offered a pointed assessment of the Duchess of Sussex’s transition from actress to royal to television host while discussing Markle’s Netflix series, "With Love, Meghan."

When asked about Markle stepping into her space with a cooking and lifestyle show, Stewart questioned whether the career transition made sense.

MEGHAN MARKLE RETURNS TO BRITAIN WITH PRINCE ARCHIE AND PRINCESS LILIBET FOR FIRST TIME IN YEARS

Martha Stewart questioned Meghan Markle's transition into the lifestyle television space during a recent interview. (Cindy Ord/Getty Images;Jonathan Brady / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)

"If you’re an actress, it’s hard to then transition to a princess and then from a princess into a homemaking guru on a television show," Stewart told People. "It doesn’t sort of follow. So go from there."

Stewart also revealed that she recently crossed paths with Markle at a dinner party in California shortly after the duchess returned from a family trip to the United Kingdom.

"I had dinner with Meghan Markle the other night," she said. "We were both guests at a dinner party in California. And she had just gotten back from the palace."

Stewart said their interaction was brief.

"I didn’t talk to her really more than to say a couple words, but I know she was talking about it," she added.

Last month, Markle traveled to Britain with Prince Harry and their two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, marking the family’s first visit to England in four years.

King Charles and Queen Camilla hosted the Duke and Duchess of Sussex and their children for a private family meeting at Highgrove House in July.

The Sussexes moved to California in 2020 after stepping back as senior working members of the royal family. Markle later returned to the entertainment industry while expanding into media, business and lifestyle ventures.

MEGHAN MARKLE AND NETFLIX END LIFESTYLE BRAND PARTNERSHIP AS CRITICS SAY THEY 'GOT MARKLED ENOUGH'

Meghan Markle and Prince Harry married in 2018. (Chris Jackson)

"With Love, Meghan" premiered on Netflix in March 2025 and featured Markle sharing cooking, gardening, hosting and entertaining ideas with celebrity guests.

The series launched alongside her lifestyle brand, As Ever, which has sold products including fruit spreads, honey, tea, wine, candles and chocolate.

Stewart’s latest remarks echo comments she made in July 2025, when she was asked by Yahoo Lifestyle about Markle’s attempt to establish herself as a lifestyle authority.

"Meghan, I don’t really know very well, and I hope she knows what she’s talking about," Stewart told the outlet.

The cookbook author emphasized that credibility and experience are essential when building a connection with an audience.

"Authenticity, to me, is everything, and to be authentic and knowledgeable about your subject matter is extremely important," she said.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Martha Stewart has built one of the world's most recognizable lifestyle brands. (Getty Images for Friends of Hudson River Park)

Stewart added that she did not object to other celebrities entering the lifestyle industry, offering a brief message to those following in her footsteps.

Stewart built her own homemaking empire after launching a catering business and publishing her first cookbook, "Entertaining," in 1982.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

Her brand later expanded into magazines, television programs, books, retail partnerships and home products. She became the first self-made female billionaire in the United States in 1999.

The Netflix series ran for two seasons and was followed by a holiday special.

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, relocated to California in 2020. (Karwai Tang)

In March 2026, Netflix and Markle announced they were ending their partnership involving As Ever, with the duchess continuing to operate the lifestyle brand independently.

"Meghan’s passion for elevating everyday moments in beautiful yet simple ways inspired the creation of the As Ever brand, and we are glad to have played a role in bringing that vision to life," a Netflix spokesperson told Fox News Digital at the time.

"As it was always intended, Meghan will continue growing the brand and take it into its next chapter independently, and we look forward to celebrating how she continues to bring joy to households around the world."

In its own statement to People, As Ever said it was "grateful for Netflix’s partnership through launch and our first year."

"We have experienced meaningful and rapid growth, and As Ever is now ready to stand on its own," the statement continued. "We have an exciting year ahead and can’t wait to share more."

Fox News Digital has reached out to Archewell for comment regarding Stewart’s remarks.

Danielle Minnetian is an Entertainment Production Assistant for Fox News Digital covering celebrity news, entertainment trends and pop culture.

articles.title: Counterterrorism expert warns Abdul El-Sayed Senate bid raises homeland security concerns

Homeland Security analyst Kyle Shideler testifies before Sen. Ted Cruz on threats including potentially from the candidacy of Abdul El-Sayed.

A Senate counterterrorism expert testified that Michigan ...
articles.body_text:
Homeland Security analyst Kyle Shideler testifies before Sen. Ted Cruz on threats including potentially from the candidacy of Abdul El-Sayed.

A Senate counterterrorism expert testified that Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed’s candidacy raises homeland security concerns because of family ties to Muslim Brotherhood-linked groups and connections to a Midwest voter-engagement organization the expert said is tied to the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR).

During a Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on Muslim Brotherhood threats in the U.S. that was boycotted by all Democrats assigned to the panel, Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, asked Center for Security Policy counterterrorism analyst Kyle Shideler if El-Sayed’s bid raised such concerns.

"Yessir, it does," Shideler told Cruz, explaining that El-Sayed’s father-in-law allegedly has connections to Muslim Brotherhood-linked groups.

"This includes being the president at one time of CAIR-Michigan," Shideler said of nephrologist Jukaku Tayeb. "Also his presence on the Islamic Society of North America Founders Committee, which is only for those most exclusively devoted to ISNA and provide significant amounts of funding."

DEMS IN THE HOT SEAT FOR SKIPPING CRUCIAL HEARING ON RADICAL GROUP HIDING IN US: 'EMBARRASSMENT'

Abdul El-Sayed, a progressive candidate in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate in Michigan, speaks during a primary election night event Wednesday, Aug. 5, 2026, at the Majestic Theatre in Detroit. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)

"There are other known [Muslim B]rotherhood members on that committee. I would also look at El-Sayed's ties to a group called Emgage, which purports to be a Muslim sort of get out the vote or candidate recruitment organization, but it has close ties to CAIR," Shideler testified.

The official bio for Emgage founding member and attorney Khurrum Wahid said the group "works to empower emerging majority communities, with a focus on Muslim Americans, to participate more in public and community and public service."

"[Emgage] was created by a former CAIR member who at one time was on a terror watchlist, and was also a consultant to convicted terrorist Sami al-Arian," Shideler said.

MICHIGAN SENATE RACE: EL-SAYED’S TIES TO EXTREMIST FUEL ANTISEMITISM CONCERNS AMONG JEWISH VOTERS

In 2012, a Times of Israel article criticized Rep. Debbie Wasserman-Schultz, D-Fla., for speaking at a fundraiser hosted by Wahid, whom it described as "currently listed on the federal terror watch list" and a legal defender of terrorism suspects.

In 2006, Al-Arian, a former University of South Florida professor who was born in Kuwait, pleaded guilty to a charge of conspiring to provide services to federally designated terror group Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ).

Fox News Digital reached out to Wahid's law firm and to El-Sayed's campaign for comment.

During the hearing, Cruz also pressed Shideler about the "Red-Green Alliance," and the prevalence of geopolitical ties between Radical Islam and the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA).

LIZ PEEK: MICHIGAN CAN STOP THE SOCIALIST FEVER RAGE — OR WATCH IT SWALLOW THE SENATE

"Does the Muslim Brotherhood also partner with political groups such as the Democratic Socialists of America?" Cruz asked.

When Cruz said the Red-Green Alliance shares hatred of Western civilization, democracy and capitalism, Shideler said he should go farther:

"It's also united around a revolutionary objective advocating for the overthrow of the U.S. Constitution."

Shideler also affirmed that the Muslim Brotherhood has active chapters or cells within the U.S.

El-Sayed has been criticized for ties to radical voices like far-left streamer Hasan Piker — who said the U.S. deserved the September 11, 2001, terror attacks — and notably declined to comment on the killing of Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei because of neighbors in heavily Muslim Dearborn who were in mourning.

articles.title: Marlins outfielders collide, knock fly ball over wall to give Braves star a home run in brutal mishap
articles.excerpt:
Two Miami Marlins outfielders ran into each other trying to catch a fly ball, knocking it over the wall for an Atlanta home run. (This video contains AI-assisted content)

The Miami Marlins outfielder...
articles.body_text:
Two Miami Marlins outfielders ran into each other trying to catch a fly ball, knocking it over the wall for an Atlanta home run. (This video contains AI-assisted content)

The Miami Marlins outfielders took the definition of outfield assist to a whole new level.

Normally, an outfield assist is credited to an outfielder when they throw a ball into the infield to record an out against a baserunner. In the bottom of the third inning of the Marlins’ 11-3 loss to the Atlanta Braves on Thursday at Truist Park, they did the complete opposite of recording an outfield assist.

With a man on first base, Braves star outfielder Ronald Acuña Jr. hammered Marlins' starter Janson Junk’s 79-mph sweeper to deep left-center field but didn’t quite get enough of it to clear the wall.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Atlanta Braves' Ronald Acuña Jr. (13) celebrates after hitting a two-run homer against the Miami Marlins in the third inning of a baseball game Thursday, Aug. 6, 2026, in Atlanta. (AP Photo/Mike Stewart)

Luckily for Acuña, Marlins left fielder Heriberto Hernández and center fielder Esteury Ruiz did not communicate about who was going to catch the deep fly ball, and they collided with each other on the warning track. When Ruiz and Hernandez collided, the ball popped up and over the wall for a home run.

The two outfielders looked around on the ground for the ball only to realize they had knocked it over the wall.

Acuña stood on first base for a couple of seconds, unsure if it was a home run before he eventually rounded the bases. Ruiz said the two outfielders couldn’t hear each other.

"When I saw the ball, I thought it was leaving the ballpark," Ruiz said through an interpreter, per MLB.com. "While I was running, I noticed it was going to stay on the field. I said, 'I got it,' and you can see in the video that (Hernández) also said, 'I got it.' But we couldn't hear each other with the noise of the ballpark. We couldn't hear each other."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Miami Marlins pitcher Janson Junk speaks with catcher Brian Navarreto in the third inning of a game against the Atlanta Braves on Thursday, Aug. 6, 2026, in Atlanta. (AP Photo/Mike Stewart)

For Acuña, it was the first of two home runs he hit in the win. He hit his second home run over the right-field wall, with no help from the outfielders, in the eighth inning to give the Braves a 9-2 lead.

"The second one was special, because the first one told me I needed help," Acuña said, according to MLB.com.

"(Acuña) had a little angel on his shoulder tonight, or something," Braves first baseman Matt Olson said, according to MLB.com.

Atlanta Braves outfielder Ronald Acuña Jr. runs after hitting a two-run homer against the Miami Marlins in the third inning Thursday, Aug. 6, 2026, in Atlanta. (AP Photo/Mike Stewart)

The Braves’ victory was their season-high eighth straight, as they continue to build on their 8 1/2 game lead in the National League East.

The Braves (70-45) will look to extend their winning streak against the New York Yankees (64-51) on Friday at 7:05 p.m. ET.

The Marlins (58-58) will look to bounce back against the Los Angeles Angels (56-59) on Friday at 7:10 p.m. ET.

Ryan Canfield is a digital production assistant for Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Mexico and Peru restore diplomatic relations after asylum row
articles.excerpt:
Former Peruvian PM Betssy Chávez was granted asylum by Mexico in November 2025

Mexico and Peru have agreed to re-establish diplomatic relations following a row over the granting of asylum to a former...
articles.body_text:
Former Peruvian PM Betssy Chávez was granted asylum by Mexico in November 2025

Mexico and Peru have agreed to re-establish diplomatic relations following a row over the granting of asylum to a former Peruvian prime minister who was charged for a 2022 coup attempt.

In a joint statement released on 7 August, Lima and Mexico City said "historic ties of brotherhood, friendship and cooperation" prompted the reconciliation.

The two countries also reaffirmed "their respect for international law and the principles of the Charter of the United Nations".

Relations broke down after former Peruvian Prime Minister Betssy Chávez sought asylum in the Mexican embassy in November 2025.

Peru cuts diplomatic ties with Mexico over ex-PM's asylum claim

Peru Congress declares Mexican president 'persona non grata'

Peruvian Foreign Minister Carlos Espá told local media outlet RPP that Chávez had been granted safe passage and had "already left Peru".

While allowed to travel to Mexico, Peru maintains the right "to request the eventual extradition" of Chávez, the Peruvian Foreign Ministry added in a statement.

Speaking at her daily media briefing, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum welcomed Chávez to Mexico as she reiterated her government's support for ousted Peruvian President Pedro Castillo.

Castillo was arrested in December 2022 on charges of rebellion, after he attempted to dismiss Peruvian congress members and install an emergency government. Hours after the attempt, Castillo was impeached.

Chávez had been imprisoned in June 2023 over her alleged role in Castillo's plan to dissolve congress. She had been released by a judge on bail in September 2025 and had denied the charges against her.

She and Castillo were both sentenced to more than 11 years in prison last November.

The restoration of diplomatic relations between Mexico and Peru comes after a new Peruvian president, Keiko Fujimori, took office last week.

articles.title: Kemi Badenoch’s weird week: defence of ex-neo-Nazi raises questions over Tory direction
articles.excerpt:
Some in party are delighted by leader’s tack rightwards but opponents have savoured latest Conservative controversy

There was a moment in the middle of this week when a news alert raised eyebrows amo...
articles.body_text:
Some in party are delighted by leader’s tack rightwards but opponents have savoured latest Conservative controversy

There was a moment in the middle of this week when a news alert raised eyebrows among the politically committed. It read: “Kemi Badenoch: Former neo-Nazi candidate would just be sorting out bins.” It was a collection of words that might prompt palpitations in the most sanguine of communications professionals, followed by panicked advice that retreat was necessary. But as a deeply weird week for the Conservative party came to a close on Friday, its leader appeared adamant she would hold the line.

With Badenoch accused of aping Reform UK on policy and purging centrists from her party in recent weeks, her decision to stand by a man who was jailed after creating sexualised images of a Jewish MP and calling her a “rodent” has prompted concerns about the leader of the opposition’s political antennae and the Tories’ wider strategy.

On Monday it emerged that Joshua Bonehill-Paine, a former neo-Nazi activist convicted of the sexist and antisemitic harassment of the Labour peer Luciana Berger, had been selected as a Conservative candidate for a local election in Somerset.

A little over 48 hours later, Bonehill-Paine – creator of pro-right viral AI clips that often depict politicians on the left in an ugly light – withdrew his candidacy, saying Badenoch had instead asked him to become an adviser to the party’s culture and integration commission, focusing on how young men become radicalised.

As pressure mounted, Badenoch said she was “sad” that Bonehill-Paine felt he “won’t be given the space to explain his position and represent his community”, chastising those who had called her judgment into question.

“Piling on [people who have changed] and trying to get them cancelled may be sport for other parties,” she wrote on social media. “But this is a different Conservative party.”

Her stance has left some in her party delighted by her persistent pugilism but others scratching their heads and looking to the door. For opponents, it has been a moment to savour, with Reform saying her support “beggars belief”, while locally focused Liberal Democrats delighted in criticising Badenoch’s insistence that as a councillor Bonehill-Paine would only have been “looking at parking, sorting out bins”.

The embrace of Bonehill-Paine has come at a critical moment in Badenoch’s leadership. Last month she embarked on a purge of the Conservative parliamentary party, writing in the Telegraph that it was “not a retirement home for failed politicians” and warning that anyone who supported net zero targets or Britain’s membership of the European convention on human rights (ECHR) would be blocked from standing as a candidate in the next election.

The former minister Gavin Barwell lost the whip, and another former cabinet member, Grant Shapps, was blocked from standing again for the party. Sources said multiple Reform members had been blocked from joining the party. “To do that while welcoming this chap has definitely raised a few eyebrows,” one source said.

The purge had left many young Tories and centrists politically homeless, said the former Tory activist Cody Butler, who resigned last weekend as chair of the One Nation Conservative Network and left the party. He said centrists, members worried about the climate crisis and conservation, and remainers – those who Margaret Thatcher may have referred to as “Wets” – were “running out of road”.

“We keep hearing the parliamentary party has never been more united,” Butler said. “But I think the real truth is the arsonists have taken control, and they’re trying to set the great oak tree of Toryism alight.”

Badenoch also announced this week that a Conservative government would evict foreign nationals with leave to remain from social housing, prompting Reform’s Zia Yusuf to accuse her of trying to copy his party’s policy, and the homelessness charity Shelter to warn the policy would “drive up homelessness and put extreme pressure on councils”.

Despite the private worries of some in the Tory party, delight in Badenoch’s unabashed tack rightwards is not difficult to find among the rank and file. “It’s going down really well,” said one MP. “The party thinks Kemi is doing brilliantly.”

A senior Conservative adviser said the party was being clear on what it believed and why. “At the last election, voters would tell us they didn’t know what the party stood for. Kemi is changing that,” they said.

But rightwingers are not the only ones enjoying the ride. Labour sources said they had been looking on and reaching for the popcorn this week. “Just as you think Kemi might finally be sorting out their tent, she spends a week focused on totally irrelevant nonsense,” said one. “Nothing trumps a person’s instincts and hers are just wrong.”

In the yellow corner, gleeful Lib Dems point out that under Badenoch the Tories seem to be showing little interest in taking back any of the 60 seats they lost directly to their party in 2024 as part of a drubbing in which the Conservatives shed a record 251 seats.

Once the near unchallenged flagbearer of middle England, the Conservatives now have zero MPs in Oxfordshire, for the first time since 1777. A committed leftwing hiker could walk from Land’s End to London without passing through a Tory constituency. Despite Badenoch’s insistence that the May local elections showed “the Conservatives are coming back”, the party lost about 500 councillors in England and ceded control of three local authorities. Even now, the Tories are skittering along at 19% of the vote, compared with Reform on 24 and Labour on 23, according to Politico’s poll of polls.

A senior Lib Dem source said: “It was widely expected that the Conservatives were at their lowest ebb in 2024 and would quickly start making progress. In fact, it’s us that have taken loads off them rather than the other way round.

“Whether it is [on] fighting for more action on the climate or defending human rights, the Conservatives sound more like Nigel Farage than former leaders who were popular with middle England. It is genuinely giving us the biggest opportunity against them we have ever had.”

Given current polling – and the results of the 2024 election in which the Conservatives lost about a third of their votes to Reform – attempting to woo those who voted for Farage was logical, said the pollster John Curtice. “The Tories are in a pretty dire state but not quite as dire as they were a few months ago,” he said. “By my calculation, they are now losing around 17% of those votes to Farage.”

Polling indicates Badenoch’s personal approval rating is on the up: a YouGov poll last month put her net favourability at -11, the highest of any Conservative leader in more than five years.

Curtice said the Tories were facing a dilemma: whether to try to build a more centrist coalition with the voters who had stuck with the party, or try to win back Reform voters. “But in [Reform] voters’ minds they are the party who failed to deliver Brexit properly and who created the Boris wave,” he said. “And the more fundamental problem is not to do with ideology, it’s to do with competence. Partygate trashed their ethical reputation, and [Liz] Truss trashed their reputation on the economy.”

Robert Hayward, a Conservative peer and polling analyst, played down the theory that Badenoch was increasingly moving the Conservatives to the right but said she would have to adapt against a Labour party under Andy Burnham.

Asked where it currently looked as if the Conservatives would gain seats on their current trajectory, Hayward was candid. “I don’t think that is very clear as yet, and that’s a major challenge to the party,” he said.

“But it’s a problem for everyone. People’s allegiance to any political party is weaker now than at any moment during my lifetime. Who knows where we’ll be in December 2026, never mind on the eve of a general election.”

articles.title: Left-leaning comedian labeled 'childish' by conservative Jeff Dye after insult scrawled on Tesla
articles.excerpt:
Comedian Jeff Dye sat down with Fox News Digital and explained why he’s leaving California for Texas and how politics have increasingly influenced the stand-up comedy world.

Comedian Jeff Dye fired b...
articles.body_text:
Comedian Jeff Dye sat down with Fox News Digital and explained why he’s leaving California for Texas and how politics have increasingly influenced the stand-up comedy world.

Comedian Jeff Dye fired back after catching fellow performer Laura Kightlinger scrawling an insult across his Tesla, blasting her conduct as "inappropriate for a 60-year-old" woman.

Dye took to X Monday, where he posted snapshots from video he said was captured by his Tesla’s security cameras showing a fellow comedian he’d performed with writing an insult in the fog on his windshield.

"Performed on a show with a comic I’ve never met. Her name is Laura Kightlinger @KingKightlinger. She seemed nice enough. We didn’t talk and she left before I went up," Dye wrote, adding, "I’m assuming she didn’t know it was my Tesla she wrote ‘Douche’ on my Tesla. Strange behavior for a 60-year-old adult. Look forward to working with you again."

ROGAN TELLS ‘TRAITOR’ COMEDIANS CONDEMNING THE KEVIN HART ROAST TO ‘F--- ALL THE WAY OFF’

Comedian Jeff Dye performs at the Stress Factory Comedy Club on June 18, 2026, in New Brunswick, N.J. (Bobby Bank/Getty Images)

The photos gained traction online, with over 440,000 views. Dye posted a follow-up noting that if he’d written something similar on her car, she would’ve spent the next 3 weeks talking about how ‘women are treated differently in Comedy,’ and how even in her own business she ‘doesn’t feel safe.’"

Kightlinger is a writer and comedian, known for serving as a consulting producer on "Will & Grace" and for having several half-hour specials on Comedy Central and HBO. She appeared to endorse Senator Bernie Sanders for President in the 2016 U.S. presidential election.

Dye is an outspoken conservative, and told Fox News Digital in December that he’s "always been more conservative than my comedic counterparts. I've always been way more religious as far as like, I'm a Christian, so that's not a huge, popular thing in stand-up comedy. I was on the front lines in that way."

Following Dye’s post on X, Kightlinger posted her side of the story and a photo of the word she wrote on the windshield alongside screenshots of messages she’d since sent Dye.

CONAN O'BRIEN, ZACH GALIFIANAKIS SAY IT'S A 'MISCONCEPTION' THAT COMEDY SHOWS ONLY TARGET CONSERVATIVES

"I was so annoyed by his taking down of a comic who had just performed I impulsively wrote douche in the fog on his car. The way you’re crying out about it should be embarrassing to tough-guy misogynists everywhere," Kightlinger responded.

The screenshots reveal she also apologized on social media, calling the decision "impulsive" and noting she should’ve brought her concerns to Dye directly. The messages show Dye arguing the comedian he’d spoken about "can take a joke," and calling Kightlinger’s actions "childish behavior."

KELSEY GRAMMER SUSPECTS HE 'MAY HAVE' LOST HOLLYWOOD ROLES DUE TO CONSERVATIVE VIEWS

He also directly responded to her on X again, adding, "Im not ‘Crying out’. Im simply holding you accountable for your bulls---. I’m also not a tough guy or a misogynist. I’m simply a fellow comedian that didn’t appreciate being called a name. I’d thought you’d understand that."

When reached for comment, Dye’s management gave Fox News Digital a statement from the comedian, noting his car was not vandalized other than the writing in the fog: "My car was not vandalized and my only motivation in posting the video online was to hold Laura Kightlinger accountable for being an a------."

"Writing insults on people’s property is a totally expected behavior for fatherless teens but inappropriate for 60 year old women," Dye added in the statement.

Entertainment reporter and host of the "Hollywood in Toto" podcast, Christian Toto, echoed that sentiment. He told Fox News Digital that the back-and-forth highlights partisan friction in the industry.

"Comedians in recent years, it's almost like they're picking sides in a way," Toto said, later adding that conservative comedians are often used to the criticism.

"When you're a right-leaning comedian, you expect some blowback. So it's not exactly unique territory for him," he said of Dye.

Toto added that while sharp elbows and teasing are standard protocol among comics, in some ways this incident broke traditional boundaries.

"If you're a comedian, you've got all the tools to fire back on stage, on social media or even in person," Toto said, later comparing that kind of exchange to "trash talking on the NBA court."

"The fact that she chose a different path, I don't think that suits her well," he added.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Jeff Dye sat down with Fox News Digital in December and discussed his decision to leave California for Texas. (Photo Courtesy of SA Ent. Group)

Fox News Digital also reached out to Kightlinger’s team for comment, but did not immediately hear back.

Madison Colombo is a writer for Fox News Digital’s Flash, Media, and Culture team, covering daily breaking news and trending topics with an award-winning background in broadcast and digital journalism.

articles.title: Jose Altuve's dominant history against Robbie Ray makes him a top player prop in Padres vs Astros
articles.excerpt: Former MLB catcher Raffy Lopez joins 'Saturday in America' to discuss league's warnings regarding uniform alterations. Lopez discusses how MLB warned Giants players for bible verses, but allowed other...
articles.body_text:
Former MLB catcher Raffy Lopez joins 'Saturday in America' to discuss league's warnings regarding uniform alterations. Lopez discusses how MLB warned Giants players for bible verses, but allowed other messages, sharing his personal faith journey.

We had the first football game of the season yesterday. Okay, so not really the actual season, but it was the official first preseason game of the NFL year, and we now have something like 20 straight weeks of football on Thursday nights from here on out. I don't know about you, but I can't wait. This has been a good baseball season, but football is still the king of sports. In order to build up our bankroll for the season, we should get some cash on this Astros and Padres game.

The Houston Astros are 59-57 for the season and currently sitting in first place in the AL West. It makes almost no sense to me that Houston would be in this position. I'm not surprised they are roughly a .500 team. Based on their roster, and their pitching especially, that checks out. What is surprising is that the Mariners (or even the Rangers) haven't taken over the division from them. The Astros still have the American League MVP, and maybe that's all they need in order to get the division this year.

Jose Altuve #27 of the Houston Astros looks on after striking out during the fifth inning of the game against the Los Angeles Dodgers at Daikin Park on May 05, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) (Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images)

I mentioned there have been issues with their pitching staff, and they even traded away a couple of guys before the trade deadline. I don't really think they took back any starter of substance, though. Today, for example, they are starting Ronel Blanco, who has only pitched in 14.2 innings this season. In the three games that he has pitched, he has given up at least three earned runs, walked at least two hitters, and allowed at least one homer. The most he pitched in any game was 5.1 innings. Padres hitters haven't seen Blanco much, with only three players ever facing him, and they are a combined 0-for-9.

The San Diego Padres are once again a disappointment. Did that prevent me from betting on them to win the World Series? Absolutely not. I generally think that talent wins out, and the Padres do have talent. The Dodgers have more talent than anyone, but the Padres' roster stacks up fairly well, even if their team is underperforming once again. Their best hitters are struggling this season, but if they can all lock in, San Diego can go on a tear like Boston has this season.

The San Diego Padres logo is displayed on the field at PETCO Park before a game against the St. Louis Cardinals on April 3, 2024, in San Diego, California. (Brandon Sloter/Getty Images)

For whatever reason, it just never all seems to click at the right time for the Padres. Maybe I just overvalue their players for some reason. They once again went out and added to their team in hopes of making the push for the World Series. They traded for Robbie Ray, who starts tonight. Ray comes to them with a 10-6 record, 3.08 ERA, and a 1.29 WHIP. At his best, Ray is Cy Young-caliber. At his worst, he is still a really strong and reliable pitcher. He is coming off of two fantastic months of work, allowing just 11 runs in his past 60 innings. The Astros have been good against Ray in the past, owning a 17-for-54 history.

The majority of the damage from the Astros has come from Jose Altuve. It probably makes sense to put a player prop on him to get 2+ total bases against Ray. He is 11-for-20 against him with six extra-base hits. Even better, Altuve has only struck out once against him, so he is putting the ball in play when he faces Ray.

Fernando Tatis Jr. of the San Diego Padres runs in from the outfield during a game against the Washington Nationals at Nationals Park in Washington, D.C., on July 20, 2025. (G Fiume/Getty Images)

In addition to the player prop, I will take the Padres to win this game. Ray has been locked in, and I really don't think the Astros are that good of a team. If you can count on the Padres anywhere, it is certainly at home they are 32-25 in San Diego for the season. Give me the Padres to win this one at -126.

articles.title: Cambridge University professor resigns after major plagiarism accusations prompt investigation
articles.excerpt: Nikki Neily of Defending Education warns against controversial teacher training programs in over 20 states that push radical theories, undermining parental authority. She argues these programs use stu...
articles.body_text:
Nikki Neily of Defending Education warns against controversial teacher training programs in over 20 states that push radical theories, undermining parental authority. She argues these programs use students as child soldiers for social change.

University of Cambridge sociology professor Jason Arday resigned Wednesday after the university announced an investigation into his academic qualifications and honorary appointments amid plagiarism accusations, with one accuser telling Fox that Arday had been hired to be the "face of DEI."

Accusations against Arday surfaced last month from former Cambridge philosophy researcher Nathan Cofnas, who published a Substack article alleging that Arday was a known "plagiarist and fabulist" for more than a year, and much of his personal biography was questionable.

"I am disappointed that Jason Arday resigned. He was hired by Cambridge to be the face of DEI, and he was doing a great job," Cofnas told Fox News Digital.

Cofnas first expressed doubt about Arday's background after the educator said he had been nonverbal until age eleven and practically illiterate until 18 while still being able to get a Ph.D in 2015 and become the youngest Black professor at Cambridge University in 2023.

NEW YORK MAGAZINE COLUMNIST ACCUSED OF PLAGIARISM BY FELLOW REPORTERS, TRIGGERS INTERNAL REVIEW

Cambridge University sociology professor Jason Arday was accused of plagiarizing several papers, including his 2015 dissertation. (iStock)

Using the plagiarism-detection program, Copyleaks, Cofnas said he found several examples of Arday directly lifting materials from a 2009 dissertation without proper citation and sometimes even retaining copy-editing mistakes. Other earlier papers written by Arday were also issued corrections to add more citations, which Cofnas characterized as an admission of plagiarism.

From his research, Cofnas accused the university of hiring Arday to push diversity politics and has since been attempting to cover up plagiarism accusations to protect him from scrutiny.

"When you take away the work that is plagiarized or not otherwise written by Arday, there is essentially nothing resembling real scholarship," Cofnas wrote. "There is no indication that Arday is familiar with even elementary statistics. His research involves reporting his own experiences of alleged racism or having conversations with people and providing subjective commentary."

Arday's appointment in 2023 received massive media attention, with much of it celebrating it as a landmark moment.

Other media outlets and academics began reporting on the accusations, however, such as the Telegraph, the Guardian and the Times of London. Cambridge University initially stood by Arday in a statement on Sunday, saying Arday had already been investigated by Liverpool John Moores University and other journals for plagiarism. However, by Wednesday, Cambridge announced it was reversing course.

HARVARD CHIEF DEI OFFICER ACCUSED OF 40 COUNTS OF PLAGIARISM, INCLUDING LIFTING FROM HER OWN HUSBAND: REPORT

University of Cambridge announced an investigation into Jason Arday on Wednesday. (Igor Golovniov/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Image)

"The University of Cambridge has begun an investigation following new information about Professor Arday’s academic qualifications and honorary appointments. In order to ensure a fair process, we will not comment further until this has concluded," the statement read.

Shortly after the statement was released, Arday released his own statement through the Good Law Project announcing that he was resigning with "immediate effect," noting "public scrutiny" as a factor.

"Sadly, the years since my appointment have also been marked by an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack. While criticism is an inevitable part of academic life, what I have experienced has gone far beyond scholarly disagreement. The relentless accusations, speculation and public commentary have taken a profound toll on me and on those I love," Arday wrote.

HARVARD ATTEMPTING TO ‘REDEFINE’ PLAGIARISM TO PROTECT EMBATTLED PRESIDENT CLAUDINE GAY, ALLEGED VICTIM SAYS

He continued, "I have tried to continue because I believe deeply in the values of higher education, in rigorous scholarship, and in the transformative power of universities. I have tried because of my students, my colleagues and the countless people who have written to tell me that my journey gave them hope. But there comes a point when the personal cost becomes too great."

Arday announced on Wednesday that he would be leaving the university effective immediately. (Tu xa Ha Noi via Getty Images)

Fox News Digital reached out to Cambridge University and Arday for comment.

Cofnas added to Fox News Digital, "However, given that he is gone, a number of people have suggested that his professorship should be given to me. If the Cambridge administration could arrange this, it would go a long way toward restoring trust in higher education."

Cofnas was ousted from Cambridge in 2024 amid criticism of his writing that Blacks would almost completely "disappear from almost all high-profile positions outside of sports and entertainment" in a world of full meritocracy.

Lindsay Kornick is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to lindsay.kornick@fox.com and on Twitter: @lmkornick.

articles.title: Vehicle narrowly avoids slamming into driver on side of Ohio highway, dramatic video shows
